30:1: Abu Ja`far said: We have previously explained the meaning of His statement, Alif, Lam, Meem, and we mentioned the statements of the people of interpretation regarding it, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. Abu Ja`far said: The translators of the Qur’an differed in their interpretation of the words of God Almighty: Alif, Lam, Meem. Some of them said: It is one of the names of the Qur’an. Those who said that mentioned: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Alif, Lam, Meem, he said: It is one of the names of the Qur’an. Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim Al-Amili told me: Abu Hudhayfah Musa bin Mas`ud told us: Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Alif, Lam, Meem is one of the names of the Qur’an. Al-Qasim bin Al-Hasan told us: Al-Hussein bin Dawud told us: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Alif, Lam, Meem is one of the names of the Qur’an. Some of them said: They are opening verses with which God opens the Quran. Those who said this were: Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm al-Kufi told me: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharbi told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Alif, Lam, Meem are opening verses with which God opens the Qur’an. Ahmad bin Hazim Al-Ghafari told us: Abu Naim told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Alif, Lam, Meem are opening letters. Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me: Ishaq bin Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Adam, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Alif, Lam, Meem, Alif, Muḥammad, and Sad are the opening letters with which God began. Al-Qasim bin Al-Hasan told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, like the hadith of Harun bin Idris. Others said: It is the name of the Surah. Those who said this are: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said: Abdullah bin Wahb told us, he said: I asked Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam about the words of God: “Alif, Lam, Meem. This is the Book,” and “Alif, Lam, Meem. This is a revelation,” and “Alif, Lam, Meem. That is the name of the chapters.” He said: My father said: They are only the names of the chapters. Some of them said: It is the greatest name of God. Those who said this are: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us: Shu’bah told us: I asked al-Suddi about Ha Meem, “Ta Seen Meem,” and Alif Lam Meem. He said: Ibn Abbas said: They are the greatest name of God. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Abu al-Nu’man told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ismail al-Suddi, on the authority of Murrah al-Hamadani, who said: Abdullah said: He mentioned something similar. Al-Muthanna told me: Ishaq bin Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Musa, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: The openings of the surahs are among the names of God. Some of them said: It is an oath by which God swears, and it is one of His names. Those who said this were: Yahya bin Othman bin Saleh Al-Sahmi told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: It is an oath by which God swears, and it is one of the names of God. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Khalid Al-Hadha’ told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Alif, Lam, Meem is an oath. Some of them said: It is a collection of letters separated from nouns and verbs, each letter having a meaning different from the meaning of the other letter. Those who said this are: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki` told us, and Sufyan ibn Waki` told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ata` ibn al-Sa`ib, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Alif, Lam, Meem. He said: I, God, know best. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaid, who said: Abu Al-Yaqzan narrated to us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, who said: His statement, Alif, Lam, Meem, he said: I, God, know best. Musa bin Harun Al-Hamdani told me: Amr bin Hammad Al-Qannad told us: Asbat bin Nasr told us, on the authority of Ismail Al-Suddi in a report he mentioned, on the authority of Abu Malik, and on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and on the authority of Murrah Al-Hamdani, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Alif, Lam, Meem. He said: As for Alif, Lam, Meem, it is a letter derived from the letters of the spelling of the names of God, may His praise be exalted. Muhammad ibn Muammar told us: Abbas ibn Ziyad al-Bahili told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: Alif, Lam, Meem, “Ha, Meem,” and Nun, he said: It is a disconnected noun. Some of them said that they are letters of the alphabet that were placed. Those who said that were mentioned: It was narrated on the authority of Mansur ibn Abi Nuwayrah, who said: Abu Saeed al-Mu'addab narrated to us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The opening letters of all the surahs, Qaf, "Sad, Ha Meem, Ta Seen Meem, Alif Lam Ra," and others, are a fabricated spelling. Some of them said: They are letters, each of which includes various different meanings. Those who said that were mentioned: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim Al-Tabari told me: Ishaq bin Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar Al-Razi, who said: My father told me, on the authority of Al-Rabi bin Anas, regarding the statement of God, the Most High: Alif, Lam, Meem, he said: These letters, from the twenty-nine letters, are spoken by all tongues. There is not a letter among them that is not a key to one of His names. There is not a letter among them that is not related to His favors and trials, and there is not a letter among them that is not related to the duration of a people and their appointed times. Jesus, son of Mary, said: And it is strange that they speak of His names and live in His provision, so how can they deny Him? He said: The Alif is the key to His name: God, the Lam is the key to His name: Latif, and the Mim is the key to His name: Majeed. The Alif is the favors of God, the Lam is His kindness, and the Mim is His glory. The Alif is years, the Lam is thirty years, and the Mim is forty years. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, something similar. Some of them said: These are letters from the abjad numeral system. We were reluctant to mention the one who narrated this, as the one who narrated it was someone whose narration and transmission were not reliable. A similar narration has already been reported from Al-Rabi' ibn Anas. Some of them said: Every book has a secret, and the secret of the Qur’an is its openings. As for the Arabists, they differed about the meaning of that. Some of them said: They are letters from the alphabetical letters, and mentioning what was mentioned of them at the beginnings of the surahs dispensed with mentioning the rest of them, which are the completion of the twenty-eight letters, just as the informant dispensed with mentioning what he reported that there are twenty-eight letters in the alphabet by mentioning A B T Th, without mentioning the rest of its letters, which are the completion of the twenty-eight. He said: Therefore, that book was raised, because the meaning of the speech is: Alif, Lam, and Mim are from the separate letters, that is the book which I have revealed to you all together, there is no doubt about it. If someone says: A B T Th has become like a noun in the letters of the alphabet, just as Al-Hamd was the name of the Opening of the Book. It was said to him: Since it was permissible for a speaker to say: My son is in Ṭā Ḍaḥ, and it was known from his saying that if he said it that he wanted to report about his son that he was in the disconnected letters, it was known from that that Ṭā Ḍaḥdoes not have a name, even if that was more effective in mentioning than the rest of them. He said: The difference between mentioning the letters of the alphabet in the openings of the surahs is that they are mentioned at their beginnings differently, and they are mentioned when they are mentioned at their beginnings, which are A B T Th, together, in order to separate the report about them if what is meant by mentioning what is mentioned from them differently is to indicate connected speech and if what is meant by mentioning what is mentioned from them together is to indicate the separate letters specifically. And they cited as evidence for the permissibility of the saying of the speaker: My son in T Z and the like, from the report about it that it is in the letters of the alphabet, and that this is from his saying in the statement that it takes the place of his saying: My son in A B T Th in the rajaz of some of the rajaz poets of Banu Asad: When I saw her matter in Hatti and I joked about her lying and flattery I took from her the horns of the Shamat, and she has not left me with her and her giving Even the head was covered with blood He claimed that he meant by that the report about the woman that she was in Abu Jad, so he made his statement: When I saw her matter in Hatti, in place of his report about her that she was in Abu Jad, since that was from his statement, indicating to his listener what his statement: When I saw her matter in Abu Jad indicates to him. Others said: Rather, it was started with this at the beginning of the surahs to open the ears of the polytheists to listening to it, as they had advised each other to turn away from the Qur’an, so that when they listened to it, the composition of it would be recited to them. Some of them said: The letters that open the Surahs are letters with which God opens His speech. If it is said: Is there anything in the Qur’an that has no meaning? It was said: The meaning of this is that he began with it to indicate that the surah before it had ended, and that he had begun another, so he made this a sign of the break between them. This is in the speech of the Arabs, when a man among them recites poetry and says: But, a town whose people are not human He says: No, it did not stir up sorrows and grief But it is not from the verse and is not counted in its meter, but it is used to interrupt a sentence and start another. Abu Jaafar said: Each of the statements made by those whose statement we have described in this regard has a known basis. As for those who said: Alif, Lam, Meem is one of the names of the Qur’an, there are two aspects to their statement: One: That they meant that "Alif, Lam, Meem is the name of the Qur'an, just as Al-Furqan" is its name. If the meaning of the speaker is thus, then the interpretation of his statement, "Alif, Lam, Meem. This is the Book," is to mean an oath. It is as if he said: By the Qur'an, this Book, there is no doubt about it. The other of them: That they meant that it is one of the names of the surah by which it is known, just as all other things are known by their names which have signs by which they are known. So the listener understands from the speaker saying: Today I read Al-Muddaththir and Al-Nun, meaning the surahs that he read from the surahs of the Qur’an, just as he understands from him if he says: Today I met Amr and Zayd, and they know by Zayd and Amr what he met from the people. If the meaning of this is unclear to someone, he may say: How can this be so, when there are a number of surahs similar to alif, lam, meem and alif, lam-ra in the Qur’an? Names are only indicators if they distinguish between people, but if they are not distinguishing, then they are not indicators. It has been said: Although the names have become, due to the commonality of many people in one of them, not distinctive except by other meanings with it, such as adding the relation of the named to it, or its description or attribute, in a way that distinguishes it from other forms of it, they were initially established for distinction, no doubt. Then, when there is a need for the meanings that distinguish between those named by them. Likewise, in the names of the surahs, each name, according to the one who said this, was made an indication of the surah named by it. So, since the named shares in it other surahs of the Qur’an, the one reporting a surah from it needed to add to its name the named by it something that would differentiate the hearer between reporting about it and others, of a description, attribute, or other than that. So the one reporting about himself says that he recited Surat Al-Baqarah, if he calls it by its name, which is Alif, Lam, Meem: I read Alif, Lam, Meem, Al-Baqarah. And in Al Imran 3:I read Alif, Lam, Meem, Al Imran. And “Alif, Lam, Meem. That is the Book.” "And "And, 'Alif, Lam, Mim. God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining." It is as if he wanted to inform about two men, each of whose name was Amr, except that one of them was Tamimi and the other Azdi, he would have to say to the one he wanted to inform about them: I met Amr al-Tamimi and Amr al-Azdi, since there is no difference between them and others who share their names, except their lineage. This is also the case with those who interpret the disconnected letters as names of surahs. As for those who said: These are openings with which God Almighty begins His speech, they directed that to something similar to the meaning we narrated from the one we narrated that from among the Arabs, that he said: These are evidence of the end of a surah and the beginning of another, and a sign of the interruption of what is between them, just as you made rather at the beginning of a poem an indication of the beginning of it and the end of another before it. Just as we mentioned about the Arabs, when they wanted to begin reciting a poem, they would say: Rather, what stirred up sorrows and grief had been grief. But it is not from the house nor is it included in its meter, but it is used to indicate the end of one speech and the beginning of another. As for those who said: These are disconnected letters, some of which are names of God Almighty, and some of which are attributes of Him, and each letter has a meaning other than the meaning of the other letter, then they interpreted this in a manner similar to the poet’s saying: We said to her: Stand for us. She said: Stand. Don't think that we forgot to stand. Meaning by his saying: Qalata Qaf, she said: I have stopped. So by making the Qaf pronounced from Waqafa, she indicated what she meant by the completion of the word in which she stopped. So they diverted his saying Alif, Lam, Meem and the like to something like this meaning. Some of them said: The Alif is the Alif of Ana, the Lam is the Lam of God, and the Meem is the Meem of A’lam, and each letter of them indicates a complete word. They said: So the sum of these disconnected letters, if they appear with each letter of them, completes the letters of the word, Ana, God A’lam. They said: And likewise all that is at the beginning of the chapters of the Qur’an from that, so based on this meaning and this interpretation, they said: It is widespread and apparent in the speech of the Arabs that the speaker among them reduces letters from the word, if what remains indicates what was deleted from it and adds to it what is not from it, if the addition does not confuse its meaning to its listener, like their deletion in the reduction of the Tha’ from Harith, so they say Ya Har, and from Malik the Kaf, so they say Ya Mal, and the like, and like the saying of their rajaz poet: What is wrong with the oppressed? How can he not save his skin if he does not? As if he wanted to say: If he does such and such, he was satisfied with the letter ya from yaf’ala, and as another of them said: Good things come to you, and evil things come to you. He wants: evil. I don't want evil unless you He wants: unless you wish, so he was satisfied with the ta’ and the fa’ in both words, from the rest of their letters, and other similar examples that would take too long to cover in the book. And as Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub and Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad, he said: When Yazid bin Muawiyah died, Abda said to me: I do not see it except as a trial, so flee from your estate and join your family. I said: What do you command me? He said: I would prefer for you to... Ayoub and Ibn Awn said, with his hand under his right cheek, describing lying down until you see a matter that you recognize. Abu Ja`far said: He meant by Ṭadtaji`u, so he sufficed with the Ṭadtaji`u from Ṭadtaji`u. And as the other said in the addition to the statement, in the manner that I described: I say, when you fell on the hump, O my camel, you have not traveled far He wants: all of it, and as the other said: My shape and your shape are different, so stick to the short ones and lower your whites So he added a letter Ḍād, but it is not in the word. They said: Likewise, what is missing from the complete letters of each of these words that we mentioned is the completion of the letters Alif-Lam-Meem and its counterparts is similar to what is missing from the speech that we narrated from the Arabs in their poetry and speech. As for those who said: Every letter of alif-laam-meem and its counterparts indicates various meanings, like what we mentioned from Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, they explained that to the same interpretation as he explained to him who said: It is based on the interpretation God knows best, in that every letter of it is some of the letters of a complete word, and its indication of its completeness suffices without mentioning its completeness, even though they disagreed with him regarding every letter of that: Is it from the word that the proponents of the first opinion claimed it was from, or from another one? They said: Rather, the alif of alif-laam-meem is from various words, and it indicates the meanings of all of that and its completeness. They said: Each letter of that was isolated, and was limited by it to completing the letters of the word, because if all of the letters of the word were made clear, the word that is made clear, in which some of these disconnected letters are some, would only indicate one meaning, not two meanings or more than that. They said: Since there is no indication in that, if all of them were made clear, except for their meaning, which is a single meaning, and since God, the Most High, intended to indicate with each letter many meanings for one thing, it is not permissible except to isolate the letter indicating those meanings, so that those addressed by it know that God, the Mighty and Sublime, did not intend to intend one meaning and indicate one thing with what He addressed them with, and that He only intended to indicate many things with it. They said: The Alif in Alif, Lam, Meem implies many meanings, including the completion of the name of the Lord, which is God, and the completion of the name of God’s blessings, which are His favors, and the indication that the lifespan of a people is one year, since the Alif in the abjad system is one. The Lam implies the completion of the name of God, which is Latif, and the completion of the name of His bounty, which is Lutf, and the indication that the lifespan of a people is thirty years. The Mim implies the completion of the name of God, which is Majestic, and the completion of the name of His Greatness, which is Majestic, and the indication that the lifespan of a people is forty years. The meaning of the speech, according to the interpretation of those who say the first opinion, is that God, may He be glorified and exalted, began His speech by describing Himself as the All-Knowing from whom nothing is hidden, and He made that a method for His servants to follow at the beginning of their sermons, letters, and affairs, and a test from Him for them so that they may deserve a great reward in the abode of recompense, just as He began with Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth (al-An’am 6:1), and other similar surahs whose openings He made praise of Himself, and just as He made the openings of some of them glorifying and venerating Himself with praise, as He, may He be glorified and exalted, said: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night (al-Isra’ 17:1), and other similar surahs of the Qur’an, the openings of some of which He made praising Himself, the openings of some of which glorifying Him, and the openings of some of which glorifying and sanctifying Him. Likewise, He made the keys to the other surahs, which begin with some letters of the alphabet, praises of Himself, sometimes with knowledge, sometimes with justice and fairness, and sometimes with generosity and kindness, in brief and concise terms, then the matters are summarized after that. According to this interpretation, the alif, lam, and mim in the places of the nominative case should be raised by each other, without his saying that book, and that book would be a predicate subject separate from the meaning of alif, lam, mim. Likewise, that in the interpretation of the statement of the one who says this second statement, is raised by each other, even if its meaning is different from the meaning of the statement of the one who says the first statement. As for those who said: They are letters from the letters of the abjad calculation without any meanings that contradict that, they said: We do not know of any meaning for the disconnected letters that can be understood other than the abjad calculation, and other than the spelling of the saying of the speaker: Alif, Lam, Meem. They said: It is not permissible for God, the Most High, to address His servants except in a way that they understand and comprehend. Since that is the case and His saying Alif, Lam, Meem does not have a rational face that could be directed to it, except one of the two faces that we mentioned, then one of its faces is invalidated, which is that it is intended by it to spell Alif, Lam, Meem. It is correct and proven that it is intended by it to mean the second face, which is the abjad calculation, because the saying of the speaker: Alif, Lam, Meem cannot be followed by the statement That is the Book, because the meaning of the statement is impossible and goes beyond reason, if “Alif, Lam, Meem. That is the Book” follows it. They also argued for their statement with the following: Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Razi narrated to us: Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me: al-Kalbi narrated to me, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah ibn Ri’ab, who said: “Abu Yasir ibn Akhtab passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was reciting the opening verse of Surat al-Baqarah 2:‘Alif, Lam, Meem. This is the Book about which there is no doubt.’ So his brother Huyayy ibn Akhtab from the Jews came and said: ‘By God, you know that I heard Muhammad reciting, in what God, the Almighty, revealed to him, ‘Alif, Lam, Meem. This is the Book.’ They said: Did you hear it? He said: ‘Yes!’ So Huyayy ibn Akhtab walked with those Jews to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: ‘O Muhammad, was it not mentioned to us that you recite, in what was revealed to you, ‘Alif, Lam, Meem. This is the Book.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Yes.’ They said: ‘Did Gabriel bring this to you from God?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ They said: God, the Almighty, has sent prophets before you, and we do not know of any prophet among them who explained what…’” His reign was prolonged and his nation did not eat except you! So Huyayy ibn Akhtab said, and he turned to those who were with him and said to them: The Alif is one, the Lam is thirty, and the Mim is forty, so that is seventy-one years. Will you enter the religion of a prophet whose reign and nation did not eat except for seventy-one years? He said: Then he turned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, is there anything else with this? He said: Yes. He said: What? He said: Alif-Lam-Meem. He said: This is heavier and longer. The Alif is one, the Lam is thirty, the Mim is forty, and the Sad is ninety, so that is one hundred and sixty-one years. Is there anything else with this, O Muhammad? He said: Yes. He said: What? He said: Alif-Lam-Ra. He said: By God, this is heavier and longer. The Alif is one, the Lam is thirty, and the Ra is two hundred, so that is two hundred and thirty-one years. He said: Is there anything else with this, O Muhammad? He said: Yes, al-murr. He said: By God, this is heavier and longer. The alif is one, the lam is thirty, the mim is forty, and the ra is two hundred. This is two hundred and seventy-one years. Then he said: Your matter has become so confusing to us, O Muhammad, that we do not know whether you have been given a little or a lot. Then they got up from him. Abu Yasir said to his brother Huyayy ibn Akhtab and the rabbis who were with him: How do you know? Perhaps he has gathered all of this for Muhammad: seventy-one, sixty-one and one hundred, two hundred and thirty-one, two hundred and seventy-one. That is seven hundred and thirty-four years! They said: His matter has become confusing to us! They claim that these verses were revealed about them: “It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book. In it are verses that are precise - they are the foundation of the Book - and others unspecific.” (Al Imran 3:7) They said: This report clearly proves the correctness of what we have said about this interpretation, and the corruption of what our opponents have said about it. The correct statement in my opinion about the interpretation of the keys to the Surahs, which are the letters of the alphabet, is that God, the Most High, made them separate letters and did not connect some of them to others, making them like all other speech with connected letters, because He, the Most High, intended by His wording to indicate with each letter many meanings, not just one meaning, as Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said. Even though Ar-Rabi’ limited it to three meanings, without anything more than that. The correct interpretation of this, in my opinion, is that each letter of it contains what Al-Rabi’ said, and what all other commentators have said about it, except for what I mentioned from the people of Arabic who I mentioned: that he directed the interpretation of this to that they are letters of the alphabet. Mentioning what he mentioned of it in the keys to the surahs suffices, without mentioning the rest of the twenty-eight letters of the alphabet, by interpreting: that these letters, that book, are collected, there is no doubt about it, for it is a false and corrupt statement, as it departs from the statements of all the companions and followers and those who came after them from the dissenters of the people of interpretation and exegesis. So it is sufficient to indicate his error, the testimony of the proof against him of the error, with the invalidation of the one who said that, as we have narrated from him, when he turned to explaining the raising of that book by saying once that each one of them is raised by its companion, and another time that it is raised by the referent of what he mentioned in his saying there is no doubt about it, and once by his saying a guidance for the righteous. This is an omission from him, based on his statement that alif, lam, mim is the subject of that book, and a departure from the statement he claimed in the interpretation of “alif, lam, mim. That book,” and that the interpretation of that is: these letters are that book. If someone were to say to us: How can one letter be comprehensive in indicating many different meanings? It was said: Just as it is possible for a single word to include many different meanings, such as their saying for a group of al-Nas 114:a nation, and for a particular moment in time: a nation, and for a devout and obedient man: a nation, and for religion and creed: a groan. And like their saying for recompense and retaliation: a religion, and for authority and obedience: a religion, and for humiliation: a religion, and for accountability: a religion, and there are many similar things that would take a long time to list, as speech is made with one word, and it includes many meanings. And likewise the statement of God, may He be praised: Alif, Lam, Meem, “Alif, Lam, Ra,” Alif, Lam, Meem, and what is similar to that from the letters of the alphabet which are the opening letters of the surahs, each letter of which denotes various meanings, encompassing all of them from the names and attributes of God, the Almighty, as the commentators have said from the sayings we have mentioned. And they are, however, the opening letters of the surahs, as those who have said so have said. And the fact that these are from the letters of the names and attributes of God, may He be praised, does not prevent them from being opening letters for the surahs. Because God, may He be glorified and praised, has opened many chapters of the Qur’an with praise and thanks to Himself, and many of them with glorification and exaltation of Him, so it is not impossible that some of them begin with an oath by Him. As for the ones whose opening letters begin with the letters of the alphabet, one of the meanings of their opening letters is that they are the opening letters of the chapters of the Qur’an. They are among what God swore by, because one of their meanings is that they are letters of the names and attributes of God, the Most High, as we have explained previously. There is no doubt that the meaning of swearing by God, His names and attributes is correct. They are among the letters of the abjad system. They are symbols and names for the chapters that begin with them. This encompasses the meanings of all that we have described, from what we have explained, from its aspects. Because if God, the Most High, had intended by this, or part of it, to indicate a single meaning from what it could bear, without all other meanings, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would have made that clear to them. This is because God, the Most High, only revealed His Book to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to clarify to them what they differed about. And in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, not explaining that, that some of its interpretations are intended by it and not others, is the clearest evidence that it is intended by all of its aspects for which it is possible. It was not impossible in the mind for any of them to be from its interpretation and meaning, just as it was not impossible for the many meanings of one word to come together, in one expression, in one statement. Whoever rejects what we have said about this should be asked about the difference between this and other letters that have a single pronunciation, yet contain many different meanings, such as nation, religion, and similar nouns and verbs. He will not say anything about one of these without necessarily saying the same thing about the other. Likewise, anyone who interprets any of these things in a way that is different from the other ways we have described should be asked about the proof for his claim, from the way that must be accepted. Then he should counter with the statement of his opponent on this matter, and ask about the difference between them: from the origin, or from what the origin indicates. So he will not say one statement without requiring the same in the other. As for the grammarians who claimed that this is similar to the saying of the poet: Rather, what stirred up sorrows and grief had been grief. And that it has no meaning, but rather it is an addition to the speech whose meaning is to throw it away, so he made a mistake in many ways: One of them is that he described God Almighty as having addressed the Arabs in a language other than their own, nor in the language of any human being. Although the Arabs used to begin their poetry with bal, it is known that they never began any of their speech with alif, lam, meem, “alif, ra,” or alif, mas, in the sense of beginning it with bal. And since that was not part of their beginning, and God Almighty only addressed them with what He addressed them from the Qur’an, with what they knew of their languages and what they used among themselves of their speech, in every verse, then there is no doubt that the path of what we have described of the letters of the alphabet, with which the beginnings of the surahs, which are openings, is the path of the rest of the Qur’an, in that He did not deviate with them from the languages they knew and used among themselves in their speech. Because if this was deviated from the path of their languages and logic, it would be outside the meaning of clarification with which God, the Almighty, described the Qur’an, when He, the Most High, said: The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart, that you may be among the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue (Ash-Shu’ara’: 193-195). How can something be made clear that no one in the world can comprehend or understand, according to the statement of the one who said this statement, and that is not known in the language of any of the created beings, according to his statement? And in God’s statement that it is a clear Arabic, there is what belies this statement, and indicates that the Arabs were knowledgeable about it, and it is clear to them. This is one of the aspects of his error. The second aspect of his error in this regard is that by attributing it to God, the Most High, He addressed His servants with something that has no benefit or meaning for them, through speech in which it is the same to address them with it or not to address them with it. This is by attributing the futility that is denied in the words of all monotheists about God to God, the Most High. The third aspect of his error is that bal in the speech of the Arabs has an interpretation and meaning, and that they include it in their speech to return to a statement that has already been completed, like their saying: It was not your brother who came to me, but rather your father, and I did not see Omar, but rather Abdullah, and similar statements, as A’sha of Banu Tha’labah said: And I will drink eight, eight, thirteen, two, and four. He continued his speech until he said: In the sitting, and the goodness of his arms is like a balloon that hits me like a finger Then he said: Rather, count this, in another verse, and mention a young man of generous nature, the most wonderful. It is as if he said: Leave this and take up another style of poetry. Rather, it only comes in the speech of the Arabs in this manner of speech. As for opening their speech with a beginning meaning of length and deletion, without indicating a meaning, that is something that we do not know of anyone who has claimed from the people of knowledge of the Arabic language and its logic, except for the one whose statement you mentioned. So that would be a principle by which the letters of the dictionary, which are the openings of the chapters of the Qur’an that were opened with it, could be likened if they were similar to it, so how is it that it is far from resembling it?
30:2: And his saying, The Romans were defeated * in the lowest part of the land. The reciters differed in their recitation of it. The majority of the reciters of the regions recited it as The Romans were defeated with a damma on the ghain, meaning: that Persia defeated the Romans. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar and Abu Saeed regarding this matter: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Jafri, on the authority of Salit, who said: I heard Ibn Umar recite: “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated.” So it was said to him: O Abu Abd Al-Rahman, over what were they defeated? He said: Over the countryside of Ash-Sham. The correct reading in our view, and the only permissible reading, is “Alif, Lam, Meem. ghalabat ar-Rum” with a damma on the ghain, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. Since this is the case, the interpretation of the statement is: Persia defeated the Romans.
30:3: God Almighty says, In the lowest land from the land of Ash-Sham to the land of Persia. And they, after their defeat means: and the Romans, after their defeat by Persia, will defeat Persia within a few years. The command belongs to God before their defeat by Persia and after "their defeat by it. He decrees in His creation what He wills, and rules what He wants, and makes whomever He wills prevail over whomever He wishes to prevail over. "And on that day the believers will rejoice * in God's victory" means: and on the day the Romans defeat Persia, the believers in God and His Messenger will rejoice in God's victory for them over the polytheists, and the victory of the Romans over Persia. "God Almighty gives victory whoever He wills" of His creation, over whomever He wills, and that is the victory of the believers over the polytheists at Badr. "And He is the Exalted in Might" means: and God is severe in His vengeance on His enemies. Nothing can prevent Him from that, and nothing can stand between Him and it. "The Most Merciful to whoever of His creation repents and returns to His obedience, that He may punish him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Sa`id, or Sa`id al-Tha`labi, who was called Abu Sa`d, from the people of Tarsus, told us: Abu Ishaq al-Fazari told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Sa`id al-Thawri, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi `Umrah, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: The Muslims loved for the Romans to defeat the People of the Book, and the polytheists loved for the Persians to defeat them, because they were people of idols. They mentioned that to Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr mentioned it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Indeed, they will be defeated. Abu Bakr mentioned that to the polytheists, and they said: Shall we make a term between us and you? If they defeat you will have such-and-such, and if we defeat you will have such-and-such? They set a term between them and him of five years. It passed and they were not defeated. Abu Bakr mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to him: Why didn’t you make it less than ten? Sa`id said: A few is less than ten. He said: So he defeated the Romans, then you were defeated. He said: That is what he said. “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated in the lowest land, but after their defeat they will overcome. Within three to ten years.” He said: Those who are defeated are less than ten. “To God belongs the command before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice in God’s victory.” Sufyan said: It reached me that they were defeated on the day of Badr. Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abaan Al-Masry told me: Musa bin Harun Al-Bardi told us: Ma'n bin Isa told us: Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Ubaidullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verse, “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated in the lowest land” was revealed... why didn’t you take precautions? Because a bit is something between three and nine. Al-Jumhi said: Wailing is betting, and that was before it was forbidden. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding His statement, “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated”… to His statement, And on that day the believers will rejoice * in God’s victory. He said: It has already happened that this happened with the Persians and the Romans, and the Persians had defeated them, then the Romans were defeated after that, and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, encountered the polytheists of the Arabs, on the day when the Romans and the Persians met, and God gave victory to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those Muslims with him over the polytheists of the Arabs, and He gave victory to the People of the Book over the polytheists of the Persians, so the believers rejoiced in God’s victory for them and the victory of the People of the Book over the Persians. Atiyah said: I asked Abu Saeed Al-Khudri about that, and he said: We met with Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists of the Arabs, and the Romans and the Persians met, so God gave us victory over the polytheists of the Arabs, and God gave victory to the People of the Book over the Magians, so we rejoiced in God’s victory for us over the polytheists and we rejoiced in God’s victory for the People of the Book over the Magians, and that is what He said: And on that day the believers will rejoice * in God’s victory. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but after their defeat they will overcome. The Persians defeated them, then the Romans were defeated. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, who said: Abdullah said: Five have passed: Ad-Dukhan, Ad-Lizam, Ad-Batsha, Ad-Qamar, and Ar-Rumuz. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, he said: The Romans have been defeated has already passed. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated”… to His saying, Most of the people do not know. He said: He mentioned the Persians’ victory over them, and the Romans’ supremacy over the Persians, and the believers’ joy at the victory of the Romans, the People of the Book, over the Persians, the people of the idols. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Ikrimah, that the Romans and the Persians fought in the lowest part of the land. They said: The lowest part of the land at that time was Adhraat, and they met there. The Romans were defeated. report of that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions while they were in Mecca. This upset them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, hated for the illiterate Magians to prevail over the People of the Book among the Romans. So the infidels in Mecca rejoiced and gloated. They met the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: You are People of the Book, and the Christians are People of the Book, and we are illiterate. Our brothers from the Persians have prevailed over your brothers from the People of the Book. If you fight us, we will prevail over you. Then God revealed: {Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated in the lowest land, but after their defeat they will overcome. Within three to nine years. To God belongs the command before and after. And that Day the believers will rejoice in God’s victory} [verses]. Abu Bakr As-Siddiq went out to the infidels and said: Are you happy with the victory of your brothers over our brothers? So do not rejoice, and may God not make your eyes happy, for by God the Romans will prevail over the Persians. Our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us of that. So Ubayy ibn Khalaf stood up and said: You have lied, O Abu Fadil. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said to him: You are a liar, O enemy of God. He said: I will give you ten she-camels from me and ten she-camels from you. If the Romans prevail over the Persians, you will be fined, and if the Persians prevail over the Romans, you will be fined for three years. Then Abu Bakr came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. He said: That is not what you said. The lesser is between three and nine. So increase the risk and give him a longer term. So Abu Bakr went out and met Ubayy and said: Perhaps you regret it. He said: No. He said: I will increase the risk and give you a longer term, so make it one hundred she-camels for one hundred she-camels for nine years. He said: I have done it. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Abu Bakr narrated: Ikrimah said: There was a woman in Persia who gave birth to none but heroic kings. Khosrow summoned her and said: I want to send an army to the Romans and appoint over them a man from your sons, so advise me which of them I should appoint. He said: This is so-and-so, and he is more cunning than a fox and more cautious than a shrike. This is Farkhan, and he is more penetrating than a spear. This is Shahrbaraz, and he is more forbearing than so-and-so, appoint whichever of them you wish. He said: I have appointed the forbearing one. So he appointed Shahrbaraz. He marched to the Romans with the people of Persia and defeated them. He killed them, destroyed their cities, and cut down their olive trees. Abu Bakr said: I narrated this hadith to Ata’ al-Khurasani, and he said: Have you not seen the land of Ash-Sham? She said: No. He said: If you had seen it, you would have seen the cities that were destroyed and the olive trees that were cut down. Then I came to Ash-Sham after that and saw him. Ata Al-Khurasani said: Yahya bin Ya`mar narrated to me that Caesar sent a man called Qutmah with an army of Romans, and Khosrau sent Shahrbaraz. They met at Adhraat and Busra, which is the nearest part of Syria to you. The Persians met the Romans and defeated them. The infidels of Quraysh rejoiced at that, and the Muslims hated it. So God revealed, The Romans have been defeated in the lowest land.... the verses. Then he mentioned a hadith similar to that of Ikrimah, and added: Shahrbaraz continued to trample them and destroy their cities until he reached the Gulf. Then Khosrau died, and report of his death reached them. Shahrbaraz and his companions were defeated, and the Romans attacked them at that time, so they pursued them and killed them. He said: And Ikrimah said in his hadith: When Persia gained victory over the Romans, Farkhan sat drinking, and he said to his companions: I saw as if I was sitting on the throne of Khosrau. report reached Khosrau, so he wrote to Shahrbaraz: When my letter reaches you, send me Farkhan’s head. So Shahrbaraz wrote to him: O king, you will not find anyone like Farkhan, for he has…” To spite and strike at the enemy, do not do it. So he wrote to him: There are men of Persia who are succeeding him, so hurry to me with his head, and return it to him. Khosrow became angry and did not answer him, and he sent a messenger to the people of Persia: I have removed Shahrbaraz from you, and I have appointed Farrakhan over you. Then he gave the messenger a small paper: If Farrakhan takes over the kingdom, and his brother submits to him, then give him this. When Shahrbaraz read the letter, he said: I hear and obey, and he got down from his bed, and Farrakhan sat down and gave the paper to him. He said: Bring Shahrbaraz to me, so he brought him forward to behead him. He said: Do not hurry until I write my will. He said: Yes. So he called for the basket and gave him three papers, and said: All this I returned to Khosrow about you, and you wanted to kill me with one letter. So the kingdom was returned, and Shahrbaraz wrote to Caesar, King of al-Rum 30:I have a need of you that the messenger cannot carry, nor the papers can reach. So meet me, and do not meet me except with fifty Romans, for I will meet you with fifty Persians. So Caesar came with five hundred thousand Roman, and he began to put spies in front of him on the road, and he was afraid that he had been deceived, until his spies came to him that he had only fifty men with him, then he spread out for them, and they met in a brocade tent that had been made for them, each of them with a knife, and they called for an interpreter between them, and Shahrbaraz said: The ones who destroyed your cities are my brother and I, with our cunning and bravery. Khosrow envied us and wanted me to kill my brother, but I refused. Then he ordered my brother to kill me, so we have both deposed him, so we will fight him with you. He said: You have both hit the nail on the head. Then one of them gestured to the other that a secret is between two people, and if it passes beyond two people it is revealed. He said: Yes. So they killed both interpreters with their knives, and God destroyed Khosrow. The report reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the day of Hudaybiyyah, and he and those with him rejoiced. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated.” He said: The Persians defeated them in the nearest part of Ash-Sham. And after their defeat they will overcome.... the verse. He said: When God revealed these verses, the Muslims believed in their Lord and knew that the Romans would prevail over the Persians. So they and the polytheists gambled over five she-camels, five she-camels, and they set a deadline of five years between them. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, was in charge of the Muslims’ gambling, and Ubayy ibn Khalaf was in charge of the polytheists’ gambling, and that was before gambling was forbidden. So the deadline was set, and the Romans did not prevail over the Persians. The polytheists asked for their gambling, so the companions of the Prophet mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: You were not entitled to a deadline of less than ten, for the bit is between three and ten. They outbid them in the gambling and extended the deadline, so they did that, and God gave the Romans victory over the Persians at the end of the bit of five years from their first gambling. That was his return from Al-Hudaybiyyah, so the Muslims rejoiced at their peace treaty that had been. And with the People of the Book’s victory over the Magians, this was one of the things that God emphasized in Islam, which is His saying: And on that day the believers will rejoice * in God’s victory... the verse) Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding His statement, “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated”… to His statement, And on that day the believers will rejoice. He said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had informed the people of Mecca that the Romans would be defeated. He said: So the Qur’an was revealed regarding that. He said: And the Muslims loved for the Romans to prevail over the Persians, because they were the People of the Book.” Ibn Wakee’ narrated: Al-Maharibi narrated to us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Aamir, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “Persia was victorious over Rome, and the polytheists loved for Persia to be victorious over Rome, and the Muslims loved for Rome to be victorious over Persia, because they were People of the Book and closer to their religion. When the verse, ‘Alif, Lam, Meem, The Romans have been defeated…’ was revealed, up to ‘within a few years,’ they said: ‘O Abu Bakr, your companion says that Rome will be victorious over Persia in a few years.’ He said, ‘He is telling the truth.’ They said, ‘Would you like us to gamble with you?’ So they pledged allegiance to him for four she-camels, up to seven years. The seven years passed and nothing happened, so the polytheists rejoiced at that, and it was difficult for the Muslims, so they mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said, ‘What do you mean by a few years?’ They said, ‘Less than ten.’ He said, ‘Go and offer them more and add two years.’ Two years had not passed before the caravans came with the report of the Romans’ victory over Persia, and the Muslims rejoiced at that, so God revealed, ‘Alif, Lam, Meem, The Romans have been defeated…’ up to His saying, ‘The promise of God, God does not fail.’” He promised. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, and Matar, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Romans have passed away. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated in the lowest land,” he said: The lowest land is Ash-Sham. And after their defeat they will prevail, he said: Persia had defeated the Romans, then the Romans were victorious over the Persians. He mentioned that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Romans will defeat the Persians. The polytheists said: This is something Muhammad is guessing. Abu Bakr said: Are you whispering to me? And wailing is grieving. They said: Yes. So Abu Bakr wailed with them, and he made the years four or five. Then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The few are between three and nine, so go back to the people and increase the wailing. So he went back to them, they said: So he wailed with them and increased. He said: The Romans defeated the Persians. That is the statement of God, “And on that day the believers will rejoice * In the victory of God. He gives victory to whom He wills” the day the Romans were victorious over the Persians. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Mu’awiyah ibn Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Umrah, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated.” He said: Defeated and were defeated. As for those who read it as the Romans have been defeated with a fatha on the ghayn, they said: This verse was revealed as report from God to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the defeat of the Romans. Who said that? Nasr bin Ali told us: Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sulayman, meaning Al-A'mash, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Abu Sa'id, who said: He said: When the day came when the Romans defeated the Persians, the believers were amazed by that, so the verse was revealed: “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated”... to the end of the verse. Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told us: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: When the day of Badr came, the Romans were victorious over the Persians, and that amazed the believers, because they were People of the Book. So God revealed, “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated in the lowest land.” He said: They had been defeated before that, then he recited until he reached, And on that day the believers will rejoice in God’s victory. And his saying, in the lowest part of the earth, I have mentioned the saying of some of them in what came before, and I will mention the saying of those who did not mention his saying. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, in the lowest part of the land, means: in the edge of Ash-Sham. The meaning of his statement, lower is: closer, and it is an active verb from closeness and nearness. Rather, it means: in the lowest part of the land from Persia, so he omitted mentioning Persia because the evidence of what appeared from his statement, in the lowest part of the land, sufficed with it. And his statement, and they, after their defeat, means: and the Romans, after the Persians defeated them, will defeat Persia. His statement, after their defeat, is a verbal noun derived from the saying of the speaker: defeated him with a defeat, so the ha’ was deleted from defeat. It was said: after their defeat, and he did not say: after their defeat because of the addition, just as it was deleted from his statement, and the establishment of prayer Al-Baqarah 2:177 - At-Tawbah 9:18 because of the addition. Rather, the speech is: and the establishment of prayer. As for his saying they will be defeated, the reciters have all agreed to open the ya in it. What is required of the reciters who read alif, lam, ghalabat al-rūm with the ghayn open is to read his saying they will be defeated with the ya closed, so that its meaning is: And after their defeat by the Persians, the Muslims will defeat them, so that the meaning of the statement is correct. Otherwise, the statement would not have much meaning if the ya was opened, because the report of what had been becomes the report of what will be, and that is the corruption of one of the two pieces of report by the other.
30:4: And his saying, in a few years, we have already mentioned the difference of opinion among the people of interpretation regarding the meaning of a few in the past, and we have presented the correct of their statements, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Khallad bin Aslam Al-Saffar told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Isa, on the authority of Abdul-Rahman bin Al-Harith, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: I asked him: What is Al-Bad’? He said: The People of the Book claimed that it is nine or seven. As for his saying, To God belongs the command before and after. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement, To God belongs the command before is the Persian rule over the Romans, and after is the Roman rule over the Persians. As for his saying, And on that Day the believers will rejoice.
30:5: With the victory of God, He gives victory to whomever He wills. We have mentioned the narration in its interpretation before, and explained its meaning.
30:6: God Almighty says: God Almighty promised, He promised that the Romans would defeat the Persians after the Persians defeated them. He put God’s promise in the accusative case as a source of His statement and after their defeat they will be victorious because that is a promise from God to them that they will be victorious. So it is as if He said: God promised that to the believers, a promise God does not break His promise God Almighty says: God fulfills His promise to the believers that the Romans will defeat the Persians. He does not break His promise to them, because there is no breaking of His promises. But most of the people do not know He says: But most of the Quraysh who lie that God will fulfill His promise to the believers, that the Romans will defeat the Persians, do not know that that is the case, and that it is not permissible for there to be a break in God’s promise.
30:7: God Almighty says: These deniers of the truth of God’s report know that the Romans will defeat the Persians, apparently, from their worldly life, and the management of their livelihoods in it, and what is good for them, but they are heedless of the matter of their afterlife, and what will save them from God’s punishment there, and do not think about it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Abu Tamila Yahya bin Wadh Al-Ansari told us: Al-Husayn bin Waqid told us: Yazid Al-Nahwi told us on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world, meaning their livelihoods, when they reap and when they plant. Ahmad bin Al-Waleed Al-Ramli told me, he said: Amr bin Othman bin Omar told us, on the authority of Asim bin Ali, he said: Abu Tamila told us, he said: Ibn Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world, he said: When do they plant, when do they sow? Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us: Sharqi told us, on the authority of `Ikrimah, regarding his statement, They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world, he said: It is the lamp or something similar. Abu Hurairah Muhammad ibn Firas al-Dab’i told us: Abu Qutaybah told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sharqi, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding His statement, They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world, he said: The lamplighters. Ahmad bin Al-Walid Al-Ramli told us, he said: Sulayman bin Harb told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sharqi, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding His statement, They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world, he said: The crocheters and the saddlers. Bishr bin Adam told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world. He said: Their livelihoods and what is good for them. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, similarly. Bishr bin Adam told me: Ad-Dahhak bin Mukhallad told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, and on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world. He said: Their livelihood. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: Outwardly from the life of this world means the infidels, they know the life of this world, but they are ignorant of the matter of religion. Ibn Wakee’ told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world. He said: Their livelihoods and what is good for them. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: They know only the outward appearance of the life of this world of its profession, its dealings, and its desires, but they are heedless of the Hereafter. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: They know when their planting will be and when their harvest will be. He said: Hafs bin Rashid Al-Hilali told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sharqi, on the authority of Ikrimah, They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world. He said: Al-Siraj and similar verses. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, he said: He spent it on her livelihood. Yunus narrated: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world, but of the Hereafter they are heedless. Others said about this: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, saying: Ya`qub al-Qummi narrated to us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, regarding His statement, They know only the outward appearance of the life of this world, he said: The devils eavesdrop and hear the word that has been revealed, which should have been on earth. He said: And they are pelted with meteors, and none escapes being burned or struck by sparks from them. He said: So they fall and never return. He said: And what he heard is pelted to his human allies. He said: So they attribute a thousand lies to him. He said: So you have not seen people say, ‘Such and such will happen.’ He said: Then the truth of it comes out, as they say, what they heard from the heaven, followed by the lies they indulge in.
30:8: God Almighty says: Have these deniers of the resurrection, O Muhammad, not from your people given thought to God’s creation of them, and that He created them when they were nothing, then He transformed them through various states and times until they became men, so that they might know that He who did that is able to bring them back after their annihilation as a new creation, then He will reward the good-doer among them for his good, and the evil-doer for his evil. He will not wrong any of them by punishing him for the crime of another, nor will He deprive any of them of the reward for his deeds, because justice is not permissible. God did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with justice and the establishment of truth. And a specified term: He says: And by a fixed, specified term, when that time comes He will annihilate all of that, and replace the earth with another earth and the heavens, and they will emerge for God, the One, the Prevailing. And many people deny the eternity of their Lord and reject it, out of ignorance that their return is to God after their annihilation, and out of heedlessness of the Hereafter.
30:9: God Almighty says: Did not these Quraysh who denied God, who were heedless of the Hereafter, travel through the lands they traveled through as a trader, and look at the effects of God on the nations who came before them who denied Him, how their fate was in denying His Messengers? They were stronger than them, and they tilled the earth: He says: They extracted the earth, plowed it, and cultivated it more than these people have. So God destroyed them because of their disbelief and their denial of their Messengers. They were not able to resist, despite their great strength, the punishment that befell them from God, nor did their cultivation of the earth benefit them, when their Messengers came to them with clear signs, but they denied them, so God unleashed His wrath upon them. God would not have wronged them by punishing them for denying His Messengers and rejecting His signs, but they were wronging themselves by disobeying their Lord. And in a manner similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement: And they tilled the earth, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those before them? They were stronger than them in power and tilled the earth and populated it more than they populated it. He said: They owned the earth and populated it. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And they tilled the land, he said: They plowed it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Have they not traveled through the land... to His saying, and have plowed the earth and cultivated it, like His saying, and have left traces on the earth (Ghafir 40:21), and His saying, and have cultivated it, more than these people have cultivated, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs.
30:10: God Almighty says: Then the final fate of those who disbelieved from among those who tilled the earth and populated it, and to whom came their messengers with clear proofs from God, and they denied their messengers, so they committed evil in their actions. The worst: meaning the trait that is worse than their actions, as for in this world, it is destruction and ruin, and as for the Hereafter it is the Fire from which they will not emerge, nor will they be asked to repent. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: Then the end of those who did evil was the worst: those who associated evil: meaning the Fire. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Then the end of those who did evil was the worst, meaning: Those who disbelieved, their reward is torment. Some Arab scholars used to say: Al-Suway in this context is a verbal noun, like Al-Baqwa. Others disagreed with him on this and said: It is a noun. And His statement: Because they denied the signs of God, meaning: They were the worst offenders, because they denied the signs of God in this world, and they mocked them. He says: And they mocked the proofs of God, who were His prophets and messengers.
30:11: God Almighty says: God Almighty begins the creation of all creation alone by creating it without a partner or supporter, so He brings it into being from nothing, but by His power, the Almighty and Majestic, then He restores it as a new creation after its annihilation and destruction, just as He began it as a perfect creation, and it was nothing. Then to Him you will be returned. He says: Then to Him after He restores them as a new creation they will return, and they will be gathered for the judgment to be passed between them, and that He may reward those who do evil for what they have done and reward those who do good with goodness (al-Najm 53:31).
30:12: God Almighty says: And on the Day the Hour comes in which God will separate His creation and raise up the dead from their graves and gather them to the place of reckoning, the criminals will be in despair. That is, those who associated partners with God and acquired evil deeds in this world will despair of all evil, and they will become depressed and regretful, as Al-Ajjaj said: Hey friend, do you know a consecrated drawing? He said yes, I know it and Abelsa And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: becomes depressed he said: becomes depressed. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: The criminals will be in Hell means in the Fire. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, And on the Day the Hour appears, the criminals will be in despair, he said: The one who is in despair is the one upon whom evil has befallen. If a man is in despair, then a calamity has befallen him.
30:13: And His statement: And they will have no intercessors from among their partners means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: And on the Day the Hour will come, these criminals, whose description He, the Most High, has described, will have no intercessors from among their partners whom they used to follow, in what they called them to of misguidance, participating with them in disbelief in God and assisting in harming His Messengers, to intercede for them with God, so that He may save them from His punishment. And they were disbelievers in their partners means: And they were disbelievers in their partners in misguidance and assistance in this world against the allies of God, denying their guardianship and disavowing them, as He, the Most High, said: (When those who followed disassociate themselves from those they followed, and they see the punishment, and all ties are severed from them. And those who followed will say, If only we could have another turn, we could disassociate ourselves from them as they disassociated themselves from us) (al-Baqarah 2:166-167).
30:14: God Almighty says: And on the Day the Hour comes when creation will be gathered before God, that Day, He says, on that Day they will be separated, meaning: the people of faith in God and the people of disbelief in Him will be separated. As for the people of faith, they will be taken to the right to Paradise, and as for the people of disbelief, they will be taken to the left to Hell. Then God will distinguish the wicked from the good. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And on the Day the Hour appears, that Day they will be divided, he said: A division, and by God there will be no reunion after it.
30:15: But as for those who believed in God and His Messenger and did righteous deeds meaning: and did what God commanded them to do, and refrained from what He forbade them from they will be in a garden, rejoicing meaning: they will be among the fragrant herbs and entwined plants, and among the various kinds of flowers in the gardens, they will be happy, and will take delight in listening to music and the pleasant and comfortable life. And the Most High only mentioned the garden in this place because there was nothing more beautiful to either side, nor more fragrant than the gardens, and evidence that this is the case is the saying of A'sha of Banu Tha'labah. What a garden of the gardens of beauty, green and lush, upon which pouring rain falls The sun laughs at it, a planet in the east, full of abundant vegetation. A day more fragrant than this, nor more beautiful than this, when the origin is near So God Almighty informed them of this, that those who believe and do righteous deeds will enjoy an elegant appearance, delicious scents, and a pleasant life in what they love, are pleased with, and envy. And happiness among the Arabs means: pleasure and envy. Al-Ajjaj said: Praise be to God who gave the ink to my masters. Indeed, the Master is grateful. The commentators differed on the meaning of this. Some of them said: It means: They are in a garden where they are honored. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: They will be in a garden, being delighted, he said: They will be honored. Others said: It means: they enjoy. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, they are in happiness, he said: they are in comfort. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And they will be in a meadow, rejoicing, he said: They will be enjoying themselves. Others said: They enjoy listening and singing. Who said that? Muhammad bin Musa Al-Harsi told me, he said: Amer bin Yasaf told me, he said: I asked Yahya bin Abi Katheer, about the statement of God, And they will be in a meadow, enjoying themselves. He said: Enjoyment is pleasure and listening. Ubaidullah bin Muhammad Al-Faryabi told us: Damrah bin Rabi’ah told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, regarding his statement: They will be informed, he said: Listening is in Paradise. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Isa bin Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of the same Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Amer bin Yasaf, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Kathir, the same. All these words that we mentioned about whom we mentioned them go back to the meaning of what we said.
30:16: God Almighty says: As for those who denied the Oneness of God, belied His Messengers, and denied the Resurrection after death and the Resurrection to the Hereafter, they will be brought before God’s punishment. God has brought them to it, and He has gathered them therein so that they may taste the punishment which they denied in this world.
30:17: God Almighty says: So glorify God, O al-Nas 114:that is, pray to Him when you go to bed, which is the sunset prayer, and when you wake up, which is the dawn prayer.
30:18: And to Him be praise in the heavens and the earth He says: To Him be praise from all of His creation, without anyone else, in the heavens, from its inhabitants, the angels, and on the earth, from its people, from all kinds of His creation in it, and in the evening He says: And glorify Him also in the evening, and that is the afternoon prayer, and when you appear He says: And when you enter the time of noon. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ narrated: My father narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Razin, who said: Nafi’ ibn al-Azraq asked Ibn Abbas: Do we find the timings for the five daily prayers in the Book of God? He said: Ya-Sin 36:So glory be to God when you reach the evening Maghrib, and when you rise Fajr Dawn, and in the evening” Asr, and when you appear Dhuhr. He said: And after the ‘Isha’ prayer, there are three ‘awrahs for you (al-Nur 24:58). Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Razin, who said: Nafi` ibn al-Azraq asked Ibn Abbas about the five daily prayers in the Qur’an. He said: Yes. So he recited: So glory be to God when you reach the evening He said: The Maghrib prayer. And when you reach the morning He said: The dawn prayer. And in the evening He said: The Asr prayer. And when you reach the noon The noon prayer. Then he recited: And after the ‘Isha’ prayer there are three ‘awrahs for you (al-Nur 24:58). Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Al-Hakam Ibn Abi Ayyad, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: These two verses combine the times of prayer: So glory be to God when you reach the evening he said: the sunset and the night, and when you rise the dawn, and in the evening the afternoon “and when you appear” the noon. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Abu Ayyad, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Abu Ayyad, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: So glory be to God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning...to His statement: and when you reach the noon prayer.
