He said: The prayers were combined: So glory be to God when you reach the evening the Maghrib and Isha prayers, and when you reach the morning” the Fajr prayer, and in the evening” the Asr prayer, and when you reach the noon prayer. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ishaq bin Sulayman al-Razi told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: So glory be to God when you reach the evening Maghrib and Isha’ and when you rise Fajr and in the evening” Asr and when you appear Dhuhr. Every prostration in the Qur’an is a prayer. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So glory be to God when you reach the evening for the Maghrib prayer, and when you rise for the Fajr prayer, and in the evening for the Asr prayer, and when you reach the noon prayer four prayers. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, “So exalted is God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning. To Him be praise in the heavens and the earth, and in the evening and when you reach the noon.” He said: When you reach the evening: the Maghrib prayer, and when you reach the morning: the Fajr prayer, and in the evening: the Asr prayer, and when you reach the noon: the Dhuhr prayer.
30:19: God Almighty says: Pray at these times in which He has commanded you to pray, O people, to God who brings forth the living from the dead, that is, the living human being from the dead water, and brings forth the dead water from the living human being. And He gives life to the earth after its death, so He makes it grow, and brings forth its crops after its destruction and barrenness. And thus you will be brought forth, He says: Just as He gives life to the earth after its death, so He brings forth its crops and plants, thus He gives you life after your death, so He brings you forth alive from your graves to the place of reckoning. We have previously explained the interpretation of His statement: He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living, and we mentioned the differences of opinion among the people of interpretation regarding it, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. However, we will mention some of what we did not mention of the hadith there, God willing. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement: He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living. He said: Dead water comes forth from the human being and creates a human being from it, so that dead person is from the living, and the living person is brought forth from the dead. By that he means that He creates a human being from the water, so that living person is from the dead. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, his statement: He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living means the believer from the disbeliever, and the disbeliever from the believer. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Jarir and Abu Mu’awiyah told us on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah: He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living. He said: The sperm is the man’s semen, dead while he is alive, and the man comes forth from it alive while she is dead.
30:20: God Almighty says: And among His proofs that He is able to do whatever He wills, O people, of creation and annihilation, and of bringing into existence and annihilating, is that everything that exists is created like your father’s creation from dust, meaning by that the creation of Adam from dust. So He described them as having created them from dust, since that was what He did to their father Adam, similar to what we have explained previously of the speech of the Arabs when you address them with what you did to their predecessor, by saying: We did to you and we did. And His saying: Then you will be human beings spreading out, meaning: Then you will be a group of descendants of the one We created from human dust spreading out, meaning: you will act. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And among His signs is that He created you from dust He created Adam, peace be upon him, from dust Then, suddenly, you were human beings dispersing meaning his offspring.
30:21: God Almighty says: Among His arguments and proofs for this is also His creation of a wife for your father Adam from himself so that he might find peace with her, and that is that He created Eve from one of Adam’s ribs. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And among His signs is that He created for you mates from among yourselves. He created them for you from one of His ribs. And His statement: And He has placed between you affection and mercy, meaning: He has placed between you through marriage and circumcision affection by which you may love one another and maintain contact for its sake, and mercy by which He has made you kind to one another. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect, meaning: God Almighty says: Indeed in His action there are lessons and admonitions for a people who remember God’s proofs and evidence, and they will know that He is the God for whom nothing He wills is impossible, and nothing He wills is impossible for Him to do.
30:22: God Almighty says: And among His arguments and proofs that nothing is beyond His power, and that if He wills, He can cause to die whoever of His creation was alive, then if He wills, He can resurrect him and restore him as he was before He caused him to die. He created the heavens and the earth without anything that came about from Him, but rather with His power with which nothing He wills is impossible for Him. And the diversity of your tongues means: And the diversity of the speech and languages of your tongues. And your colors means: And the diversity of the colors of your bodies. Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge means: Indeed in His doing that like that are lessons and proofs for His creation who understand that He is not exhausted by returning them to the form they were in before their death after their annihilation. We have already explained the meaning of the worlds previously.
30:23: God Almighty says: And among His proofs against you, O people, is His determination of hours and times, and His distinction between night and day. He made the night a resting place for you in which you dwell and sleep, and He made the day a light for you to manage your livelihoods and to gather together in it from the provision of your Lord. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen. God Almighty says: Indeed in God’s action in this way, there are lessons, reminders, and evidence that nothing is beyond the power of the One who does that. He intended it for a people who listen to God’s admonitions, are admonished by them, take heed, and understand God’s proofs against them.
30:24: God Almighty says: And among His proofs is He shows you lightning, as a fear for you when you are traveling, lest it rain and you be harmed by it, and as hope for you when you are staying, that it rains and you become alive and fertile, and He sends down water from the sky meaning: He sends down rain from the sky, and with that water He revives the dead earth, so it grows and its crops come out after its death, meaning its barrenness and its being destroyed. Indeed in that are signs meaning: Indeed in His doing that are lessons and evidence for a people who understand about God’s proofs and evidence. And similar to what we said about the meaning of His statement: He shows you lightning, causing fear and hope, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And among His signs is that He shows you lightning, causing fear and hope. He said: Fear for the traveler, and hope for the resident. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the omission of an in his statement: He shows you lightning, causing fear and hope. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: An was not mentioned here because this indicates the meaning. The poet said: Oh, you who deter! I am preparing for battle and witnessing pleasures. Will you make me immortal? He said: He said: If I said what is in her people, she would not be orphaned. He prefers her in lineage and stature. He said: He means: There is no one among her people. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: If you make an clear, then it is in the nominative case, as he said: And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and your sleep. So if it is deleted, it is made min a substitute for an abandoned noun, and the verb becomes a relative clause, as the poet said: Life is nothing but two tarts, one of which I die, and the other I struggle to live. As if he meant: From them is an hour when I die, and an hour when I live. Likewise: And among His signs He shows you the sign of lightning, and a sign for such-and-such. If you wish, you can mean: And He shows you among His signs the lightning. Do not imply an or anything else. Some of those who rejected Al-Basri’s statement said: An should only be deleted from the place where it is indicated, but not in every place. As for He brought the battle, since I warned you to stand up, and I warned you to stand up, indicate the future, it was permissible to delete an, because the place is known and does not occur in all speech. As for his statement: And among His signs is that you are standing, and that you stand up, and that you stand up, this place is not deleted because it does not indicate one thing. The correct statement in this regard is that the word min in the phrase and among His signs indicates something omitted, as it comes with the meaning of partiality. If this is the case, it is known that it requires some, and therefore the Arabs omit the noun with it to indicate it.
30:25: God Almighty says: And among His proofs, O people, of His ability to do whatever He wills, is that the heavens and the earth stand by His command, submitting to Him in obedience without intention. You see, Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth, at once you will emerge. He says: When you emerge from the earth, when He calls you with a single call, responding to His call to you. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command they stand by His command without pillars Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth, at once you will emerge he said: He called them and they emerged from the earth. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, in his statement: When you come forth, he said: from the earth.
30:26: God the Most High says: “And to God belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth of angels, jinn, and mankind - slaves and angels. “All are obedient to Him.” That is, all are obedient to Him. Someone might say: How can it be said All are obedient to Him when it is known that most of mankind and jinn are disobedient to Him? We say: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that, so we will mention their differences, then we will explain what is correct in our view regarding that statement. Some of them said: That is a statement that can be interpreted as general, but what is meant by it is specific, and its meaning is: All are obedient to Him in life, eternity, death, annihilation, resurrection, and the Hereafter. None of that is impossible for Him, even if some of them disobey Him in other matters. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding His statement, And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command… to all are obedient to Him, meaning obedient, meaning life, resurrection, and death, and they are disobedient to Him in all other forms of worship. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: All are obedient to Him, acknowledging that He is their Lord and Creator. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: All are obedient to Him: meaning obedient and acknowledging that God is their Lord and Creator. Others said: It is specific, and the meaning is: He has whoever is in the heavens and the earth, of kings and servants who believe in God and obey Him, and no one else. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, All are devoutly obedient to Him, he said: All are obedient to Him. The obedient is the devout. He said: There is nothing but that it is obedient, except the son of Adam, and he is the most deserving of being the most obedient to God. And regarding His statement, And stand before God, devoutly obedient Al-Baqarah 2:238, he said: This is in prayer. Do not speak during prayer as the People of the Book speak during prayer. He said: The People of the Book walk toward one another in prayer. He said: They face each other in prayer, and when they are asked about that, they say: So that the animosity may leave our hearts and our hearts may be in peace with one another. So God said: And stand before God, devoutly obedient. Do not move away as they move away, devoutly obedient. Do not speak as they speak. He said: As for everything else in the Qur’an about devoutness, it is obedience except for this one. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the one we mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, which is that everyone in the heavens and the earth, created by God, is obedient to His actions in what He, the Most High, has willed of life and death, and the like, even if he disobeys Him in what he earns by his words, and in what he has the ability to choose and prefer over what is contrary to it. I said: This is more correct in interpreting it, because the disobedient among His creation, in what they have the means to acquire, are many in number, and the Most High has informed us about all of them that they are obedient to Him, so it is not permissible to inform us about the one who is a protector that he is obedient to Him in what he is disobedient to Him. If that is the case, then the one in whom he is disobedient is what I have described, and the one who is obedient to Him is what I have explained.
30:27: And His statement, And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, God Almighty says: The One who has these attributes, blessed and exalted be He, is the One who begins creation from nothing, so He creates it and brings it into existence, after it was nothing, then He annihilates it after that, then He repeats it, just as He began it after its annihilation, and that is easier for Him. The commentators differed on the meaning of his statement, And it is easier for Him. Some of them said: It means: And it is easy for Him. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yahya bin Saeed Al-Baytar told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of the one who mentioned it, on the authority of Mundhir Al-Thawri, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Khaitham, And it is easier for Him, he said: Nothing is difficult for Him. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And it is He who originates creation and then repeats it, and it is easier for Him, meaning: Everything is easy for Him. Others said: Its meaning is: Recreating them after their annihilation is easier for Him than creating them in the first place. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And it is easier for Him, he said: He says: Easier for Him. Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And it is easier for Him, he said: Repeating is easier for Him than starting over, and starting over is easy for Him. Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of `Ikrimah, he recited this verse: And it is He who originates creation and then repeats it, and it is easier for Him. He said: The unbelievers were amazed at God’s bringing the dead back to life. He said: So this verse was revealed: And it is He who originates creation and then repeats it, and it is easier for Him. Recreating is easier for Him than initiating creation. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ghundar told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, in a similar manner, except that he said: Recreating creation is easier for Him than starting it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And it is easier for Him: He says: Repeating it is easier for Him than starting it, and everything is easy for God. And in some readings: And everything is easy for God. This statement may have two possible meanings, other than the two statements I mentioned. It could mean: He is the One who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for creation: meaning that repeating something is easier for creation than beginning it. What we mentioned from Ibn Abbas in the report that Ibn Saad told me is also a statement of his and prepared. More than one Arab scholar has interpreted the words of Dhu al-Rummah. My brother, the translucent bones of the spines of sleep have crept into his bones, so he has submitted. It means subject, and the other says: By your life, Al-Zubayr is generous with his good deeds over the years and better He is generous to him for every blame he has delayed and for every reason of generosity he is the first. It means: and virtuous, and Ma’n said: By God, I do not know which of us death will attack first. It means: I am afraid, and the other said: Imru' al-Qais wished for my death, and if I die, then that is a path in which I am not alone. It means: I am not alone in it, and Al-Farazdaq said: He who made the sky high built for us a house whose pillars are stronger and taller It means: dear, tall. They said: And from it is their saying in the call to prayer: God is great, meaning: God is great. And they said: If someone says: God is not described with this, but rather creation is described with it. So he claimed that it is easier for creation, and the proof against him is the statement of God And that is easy for God (An-Nisa’: 30), and His statement And their preservation does not burden Him (al-Baqarah 2:255): meaning that their preservation does not burden Him. And His saying, And to Him belongs the highest example, means: God is the highest example in the heavens and the earth, which is that there is no god but Him alone, with no partner for Him. There is nothing like Him. That is the highest example. Exalted and sanctified is our Lord. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And to Him belongs the highest example in the heavens, meaning: There is nothing like Him. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And to Him belongs the highest description in the heavens and the earth, is similar to the fact that there is no god but Him, and there is no lord other than Him. And His statement, And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise, God Almighty says: And He is the Exalted in His vengeance against His enemies, the Wise in His management of His creation, and His disposition of them as He wills of life and death, resurrection and spreading, as He wills.
30:28: God Almighty says: O people, let your Lord give you an example from yourselves. Do you have any of those whom your right hands possess? He says: From your slaves, any partners in the wealth We have provided you, so you are equal in it as they are. He says: If you are not satisfied with that for yourselves, then how can you be satisfied that your gods that you worship should be partners in your worship of Me, while you and they are My slaves and slaves, and I am the owner of all of you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, “He has set forth for you an example from among yourselves: Do you have among those whom your right hands possess partners in what We have provided for you so that you would be equal therein?” He said: An example that God set forth for the one who equates any of His creation with Him, meaning: If one of you shares his bed and his wife with his slave, then likewise God is not pleased for any of His creation to equate Him with Him. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, “He has set forth for you an example from among yourselves: Do you have among those your right hands possess partners in what We have provided for you so that you are equal therein?” He said: Do you find anyone who treats his slave like this with regard to his wealth? So how can you deliberately do so while you bear witness that they are My slaves and My creation, and give them a share in My worship? How can this be? He said: This is an example that God set forth for them, and he recited, Thus do We detail the verses for a people who understand. The commentators differed in their interpretation of His statement, You fear them as you fear yourselves. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: You fear these partners among those whom your right hands possess that they will inherit your wealth after your death, just as you inherit from one another. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Concerning the gods, and in it he says: You fear that they will inherit you as some of you inherit one another. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: You fear that these partners of what your right hands possess will share your wealth with you, as you share with one another. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us: I heard Imran say: Abu Majlaz said: Your slave, do not fear that he will share your wealth with you, even though he has no right to do so. This is how God is, with no partner. The first of the two opinions is more correct in interpreting the second opinion, because it is more similar to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the words. That is that God, the Most High, rebuked these polytheists who made gods from among His creation to worship, and associated them with Him in their worship, while they nevertheless acknowledged that they were His creation and they were His slaves. He reproached them for doing that, and said to them: “Do you have partners among your slaves in what We have bestowed upon you of Our blessings? They are equal, and in that you fear that they will share with you that wealth which is between you and them, just as some of you fear that one of you will share with another the wealth which is between you and him as a partnership.” So the fear that God, the Most High, mentioned, that it is a fear of what a partner fears from his partner sharing the wealth which is between them, is more similar to a fear of him inheriting it, because mentioning a partnership does not indicate a fear of inheritance, and it may indicate a fear of separation and sharing. And His statement, Thus do We detail the verses for a people who understand, the Most High says: Just as We have made clear to you, O people, Our proofs in these verses of this Surah of Our ability to do whatever We will, of creating whatever We will, annihilating whatever We love, and restoring whatever We want to restore after its annihilation, and We have demonstrated that worship is only appropriate for the One, the Compeller, in Whose hand is the dominion over all things, thus do We make clear Our proofs in every truth for a people who understand, so that they may reflect upon them when they hear them, and take heed and learn from them.
30:29: God Almighty says: That is not so, nor do these polytheists associate with God the gods and idols in the worship of God, because they have a share in what God has provided them from the possessions of their right hands, so they and their slaves are equal in it, fearing that they will share with them what they associate with them, so they accepted for God what they were satisfied with for themselves, so they associated them in His worship. But those who wronged themselves and disbelieved in God followed their desires, out of ignorance of God’s right upon them, so they associated with gods and idols in His worship. Then who will guide he whom God has led astray? He says: So who will direct to the right path, meaning who will guide to Islam he whom God has led astray from righteousness and guidance? And they will have no helpers. He says: And who will support he whom God has led astray, to aid him and rescue him from the misguidance with which He, Almighty and Majestic, tests him.
30:30: God Almighty says: So direct your face toward the face toward which your Lord has directed you, O Muhammad, to obey Him, which is the religion, inclining toward truth. He says: Upright in His religion and obedience to Him, the nature of God upon which He created people. He says: The craftsmanship of God upon which He created people. And the word inclining toward truth is used as a source of the meaning of His statement: So direct your face toward the religion, inclining toward truth. This is because the meaning of that is: God created people upon that nature. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, The nature of God upon which He created mankind, he said: Islam has been since God created them all from Adam, they acknowledge that, and he recited And when your Lord took from the children of Adam - from their loins - their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying], Am I not your Lord? They said, Yes, we testify (al-A’raf 7:172). He said: So this is the statement of God Mankind was one community, then God sent the prophets (al-Baqarah 2:213) after that. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, The nature of God he said: Islam. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya ibn Wadh told us: Yunus ibn Abi Salih told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Maryam, who said: Umar passed by Muadh ibn Jabal and said: What is the foundation of this nation? Muadh said: Three things, and they are the salvation: sincerity, which is the fitrah the fitrah of God upon which He created mankind; prayer, which is the religion; and obedience, which is protection. Umar said: You have spoken the truth. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told me, he said: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, that Umar said to Muadh: What is the foundation of this nation? Then he mentioned something similar. His saying, There is no changing the creation of God, means: There is no changing the religion of God: that is, that is not appropriate, and it should not be done. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said something similar to what we have said about this. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, There is no change in the creation of God, he said: in His religion. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Layth, he said: Mujahid sent a man called Qasim to Ikrimah asking him about the statement of God, There is no change in the creation of God, that it is only the religion, and he recited, “There is no change in the creation of God. That is the right religion.” Ibn Wakee’ told us: Zaid bin Habbab told us, on the authority of Husayn bin Waqid, on the authority of Yazid al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah: The nature of God upon which He created mankind He said: Islam. He said: My father told me, on the authority of Nadr ibn Arabi, on the authority of Ikrimah, There is no change in the creation of God. He said: The religion of God. He said: My father told me, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: For the religion of God. He said: My father told us, on the authority of Abdul-Jabbar bin Al-Ward, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, who said: Mujahid said, Ask Ikrimah about it. So I asked him, and Ikrimah said: “The religion of God Almighty, may God disgrace him? Did he not hear His saying, ‘The nature of God upon which He has created mankind. There is no change in the creation of God.’” Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: There is no change in the creation of God, meaning in the religion of God. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: For the religion of God. He said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hamid al-A’raj, who said: Saeed ibn Jubayr said, There is no change in the creation of God. He said: In the religion of God. He said: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, There is no change in the creation of God. He said: God’s religion. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, There is no change in the creation of God, he said: God’s religion. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Misa’ar and Sufyan, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: There is no change in the creation of God. He said: in the religion of God. He said: My father told us, on the authority of Jaafar Al-Razi, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: For the religion of God. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: There is no change in God’s creation of animals by castrating the males among them. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of a man who asked Ibn Abbas about castrating animals, and he disliked it and said, There is no changing God’s creation. He said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hamid al-A’raj, who said: Ikrimah said: Castration. He said: Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Castration. And His statement, That is the right religion, means that God Almighty says: Indeed, your directing your face toward the religion, inclining toward truth, without changing or altering it, is the right religion, meaning the straight religion in which there is no deviation from the straight path, from the true faith to Judaism and Christianity, and other misguidances and innovations. Some of them have directed the meaning of religion in this context to accountability. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amara told me, he said: Abdullah ibn Musa told us, he said: Abu Laila told us, on the authority of Buraidah, That is the right religion, he said: The right reckoning. But most people do not know, God Almighty says: But most people do not know that the religion that I have commanded you, O Muhammad, with by My saying, So set your face toward the religion, inclining toward truth, is the true religion, not all other religions.
30:31: God Almighty means by His saying turning to Him repentant, returning to God, and turning to Him. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, turning to Him, he said: The one who turns to God is the one who obeys God, who turns to obeying God and His command, and turns away from the things he was doing before that. The people were disbelievers, so they turned away and returned to Islam. The interpretation of the statement: So direct your face, O Muhammad, toward the religion, inclining toward truth, turning to it to God. Al-Mayboon is a state of the Kaf in your face. If someone were to say: How can it be a state of it, when the kaf is a metaphor for one, and al-muniboon is an adjective for a group? It would be said: Because the command from the kaf is a metaphor for his name from God in this place, a command from Him to him and to his nation, so it is as if it was said to him: So direct your face, you and your nation, toward the religion, inclining toward God, turning to Him. And His statement, And fear God, means, the Most High, that you fear God and be mindful of Him, lest you neglect to obey Him and commit sins against Him. And do not be among those who associate others with God, meaning, do not be among those who associate others with God by neglecting His obligations, committing sins against Him, and disobeying the religion to which He has called you.
30:32: And His statement, Of those who divided their religion and became sects, means: Do not be among the polytheists who changed their religion, opposed it, and departed from it. And became sects, means: And they were parties and groups like the Jews and Christians. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Those who divided their religion and became sects: they are the Jews and Christians. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Those who divided their religion and became sects, to the end of the verse, he said: These are Jews. So if His statement, Of those who divided their religion, were to be interpreted as meaning that it is a new report separate from His statement, And do not be of the polytheists, and that its meaning is: Of those who divided their religion and became sects “parties,” each party rejoicing in what it has, then that would be an interpretation that the speech could bear. His statement, Every party rejoices in what they have, means: Every group and sect of those who divided their true religion and introduced the innovations they introduced rejoices in what they have. He says: in what they adhere to of the doctrine, they are happy and pleased, thinking that the truth is with them and not others.
30:33: God Almighty says: And when these polytheists who associate with God another god are touched by harm, and are afflicted with hardship, famine, and drought, they call upon their Lord meaning: they are sincere in monotheism to their Lord, and they single Him out in supplication and entreaty, and they seek His aid, turning to Him, repenting to Him for their polytheism and disbelief. Then when He lets them taste mercy from Him meaning: then when their Lord Almighty removes that harm from them and relieves them and grants them ease, fertility, and plenty, then a party of them, meaning: a group of them associate others with their Lord, meaning: they worship gods and idols with Him.
30:34: God the Most High says, threatening these polytheists, about whom He informed that if He removed their hardship they would disbelieve in Him: So that they may disbelieve in what We have given them. He says: If they associate partners with their Lord, so that they may disbelieve in: that is, deny the blessing I bestowed upon them by removing the hardship they were in and replacing it for them with ease, fertility, and well-being. That ease and abundance is what He the Most High gave them, who said when We gave them. And His statement, Then enjoy yourselves means: So enjoy, O people, what We have given you of ease and abundance in this world. For you will soon know when you come to your Lord, what you will encounter of His punishment and the great retribution for your disbelief in Him in this world. Some of them read So they will soon know with a ya, meaning: So that they may disbelieve in what We have given them. They enjoyed themselves as a statement, so they will soon know.
30:35: God Almighty says: “We sent down to those who associate gods and idols in Our worship, a book confirming what they say and the truth of what they do. “It speaks of what they used to associate.” He says: So that book speaks of the truth of their association. What He, the Most High, means by that is: He did not send down a book about what they say and do, nor did He send a messenger with it. Rather, it is something they fabricated and invented, following their whims. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Or have We sent down to them an authority so that it speaks about what they used to associate with Him? He said: That We sent down to them a book so that it speaks about their association with Him.
30:36: God Almighty says: And when people are afflicted by us with fertility and prosperity, and well-being in body and money, they rejoice in that, but if they are afflicted by us with hardship, drought, and calamity in money and body, because of what their hands have put forth meaning: because of the bad deeds they have done between themselves and God, and the sins they have committed, because then they despair meaning: when they lose hope of relief, and despair is hopelessness, and from this is the saying of Hamid al-Arqat: They found the pilgrims not despairing His saying, If they despair is the answer to the conditional clause, because if replaces the verb by indicating it. It is as if it was said: And if evil befalls them because of what their hands have put forth, you will find them despairing, or you will find them, or you will see them, or you will see them. Some of the Basran grammarians used to say: If is an answer because it is related to the first statement in the same way as fa.
30:37: God Almighty says: Have these people not seen, with the eyes of their hearts, those who rejoice when prosperity and abundance befall them, and despair of relief when hardship befalls them, and know that hardship and prosperity are in the hand of God, and that God expands provision for whomever He wills of His servants and makes it spacious for them, and restricts it for whomever He wills and makes it tight for them? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe. He says: Indeed, in His expansion of that for whomever He expands it for, and His restriction of it for whomever He restricts it for, and His difference between those of His servants who differ with Him in wealth and poverty, is a clear proof for whoever believes in God’s proofs and acknowledges them when he witnesses and sees them.
30:38: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So, O Muhammad, give your relatives their due from you in terms of kinship and kindness, and the poor and the wayfarer, what God has imposed for them in that. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: Ghundar told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, Then give the relative his right, and [also] the poor and the traveler. He said: It is that you give them their right if you are able to do so, and if you are not able to do so, then speak to them in a gentle manner, speak to them in a good manner. And His statement, That is better for those who desire the face of God, says the Most High: Giving these people their rights that God has obligated His servants to do is better for those who desire God by giving them that. And those are the successful ones, says: And whoever does that seeking the face of God with it, then those are the successful ones, the ones who attain their requests with God, the successful ones with what they sought and sought by giving them what they were given.
30:39: God the Almighty says: And whatever you give, O people, to increase people’s wealth by returning its reward to the one who gave it, will not increase with God. He says: It will not increase with God, because its owner did not give it to the one who gave it to him, seeking thereby His face. “And whatever you give in zakat” He says: And whatever you give in charity, seeking thereby the face of God. Those, meaning those who give charity with their wealth, seeking thereby the face of God, will be multiplied. He says: They are the ones who will have double the reward and recompense, from the Arab saying: The people became fat and thirsty, when their camels became fat and thirsty. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And whatever you give in interest that it may increase within the people’s wealth - it does not increase with God, he said: It is what people give to one another, a man giving a gift to another, intending to give more than that. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur ibn Safiyya, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr: And whatever you give in interest so that it may increase within the people’s wealth, he said: It is a man who gives a gift to another man in order to reward him. He said: Yahya told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur bin Safiyya, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told me, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur ibn Safiyya, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr: And whatever you give in interest that it may increase within the people’s wealth, he said: A man gives to be rewarded for it. Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And whatever you give in interest so that it may increase within the people’s wealth, he said: Gifts. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: My father told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: They are gifts. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And whatever you give in interest so that it may increase within the people’s wealth he said: He gives his money seeking something better than it. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: It is a man who gives a gift to another man, in order to reward him with something better than it. He said: Muhammad bin Hamid Al-Maamari narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father: It is the man who gives a gift and offers a present, in order to be rewarded with something better than that, for there is no reward or sin in it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And whatever you give in interest so that it may increase within the people’s wealth does not increase with God. He said: Whatever you give of something seeking a worldly reward and a recompense from people, that is the interest that God does not accept and does not reward for. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement, And whatever you give in interest that it may increase within the people’s wealth, it is what people exchange among themselves and give as gifts. A man gives a gift in order to receive something better than it, and this applies to people in general. As for his saying And do not bestow a favor, expecting more in return (al-Muddaththir 74:6), this is specifically for the Prophet. He had no right to give except to God, and he did not give in order to be given more in return. Others said: What is meant by this man is: He gives his money to a man so that he can help him himself, serve him, and benefit from him, not to seek a reward from God. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father and Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Aamer: And whatever you give in interest so that it may increase within the people’s wealth, he said: It is a man who sticks to another man, is kind to him, serves him, and travels with him, and gives him some of the profit from his wealth in order to reward him, but he only gave it to him seeking his help, and did not seek the pleasure of God. Others said: It is giving a man his money so that the money of the one who gave it to him will increase, not to seek reward from God. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And whatever you give in interest so that it may increase within the people’s wealth, he said: Have you not seen a man say to another: I will give you money, and he gives it to him? This does not increase with God, because he gives it to someone other than God so that his wealth may increase. He said: Amr bin Abdul Hamid Al-Amili told us, he said: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, he said: I heard Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i say about His statement, And whatever you give in interest that it may increase within the people’s wealth does not increase with God, he said: This was in the pre-Islamic period, when someone would give money to a relative so that his wealth would increase. Others said: This is for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifically, but for others it is permissible. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Abu Rawad, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: And whatever you give in interest to increase within the people’s wealth does not increase with God. This is for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is permissible interest. We chose the statement we chose in this regard because it is the most obvious of its meanings. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra, and some of the people of Mecca, recited it as li-yarrubu with a fat-ha on the ya’ from yarbu, meaning: And whatever you give in interest, that interest will increase in the wealth of the people. The majority of the reciters of Medina recited it as li-tarbawa with a ta’ from tarbawa and a damma on it, meaning: And whatever you give in interest, that you may increase in the wealth of the people. The correct view in this regard, in our view, is that they are two well-known readings among the reciters of various regions, although their meanings are close. This is because when the owners of wealth increase, they use the wealth for usury, and when the wealth increases, then the increase in it is usury. Since this is the case, then whichever of the two readings the reciter recites, he is correct. As for his saying, And whatever you give in zakat, desiring the countenance of God - it is those who will receive a multiplying reward, the people of interpretation said in their interpretation something similar to what we have said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And whatever you give in zakat, desiring the countenance of God - it is those who will receive a multiplying reward. He said: This is what God accepts and multiplies for them ten times its value, or more than that. It was narrated on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq, who said: Muammar informed us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His statement, And whatever you give in interest that it may increase within the people’s wealth - it does not increase with God, he said: It is a gift. One gives something away wanting to be rewarded with something better than it, so that is the one that does not increase with God. Its owner will not be rewarded for it, nor will he be sinful for it. And whatever you give in zakat, he said: It is charity, seeking the countenance of God, it is those who will receive multiples. Muammar said, Ibn Abi Nujayh said, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar.
30:40: God Almighty says to those who associate others with Him, informing them of the ugliness of their actions and the evil of their deeds: God, O people, is He to whom worship is only appropriate, and it should not be for anyone else. He is the One who created you when you were nothing, then He provided for you and empowered you, and you had no power before that. Then He will cause you to die after He created you alive, then He will bring you to life after your death for the Resurrection. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, God is He who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will bring you to life refers to the play after death. And His statement, Is there among your partners any that does any of that? God the Most High says: Is there among your gods and idols that you make partners with God in your worship of Him any that does any of that, such as creating, providing for, causing death, or resurrecting? This is a rebuke from God to these polytheists. The meaning of the statement is that their partners do not do any of that, so how can someone who does not do any of that be worshipped besides God? Then He exonerated Himself from the slander that these polytheists fabricated against Him by claiming that their gods are partners with Him, so He the Most High said, Glory be to Him: that is, sanctifying and exonerating God. And Exalted means: and high above what they associate means: above the association of these polytheists with Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Is there among your partners any who do anything of that? No, by God, Glory be to Him, and He is exalted above what they associate with Him, He glorifies Himself when slander is said against Him.
30:41: God Almighty says: Sins have appeared on land and sea because people’s hands have earned what God has forbidden them. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his statement, Corruption has appeared on land and sea. Some of them said: By land he meant the deserts, and by sea he meant the cities and villages that are on water and rivers. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Uthman told us, he said: An-Nadr ibn Arabi told us, on the authority of Mujahid, And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein (al-Baqarah 2:205)… the verse. He said: When he turns away, he strives to transgress and oppress, so God withholds rain, then “He destroys crops and animals. He does not like corruption” (al-Baqarah 2:205). He said: Then Mujahid recited, Corruption has appeared in the sea… the verse. He said: Then he said: By God, it is not your sea, but every village on running water is a sea. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Al-Nadr Ibn Arabi, on the authority of Ikrimah, Corruption has appeared on land and sea. He said: As for me, I do not say this sea of yours, but every village has running water. He said: Yazid bin Harun narrated to us, on the authority of Amr bin Farukh, on the authority of Habib bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Ikrimah, Corruption has appeared on land and sea. He said: The Arabs call the regions seas. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned, he said: This was before God sent His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was filled with misguidance and injustice, but when God sent His Prophet, some people returned. His saying, Corruption has appeared on land and sea. As for the land, it is the people of the column, and as for the sea, it is the people of the villages and the countryside. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Corruption has appeared on land and sea, he said: sins, and he recited, That He may let them taste some of what they have done that perhaps they will return. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Amir told us: Qara told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned, he said: God corrupted them with their sins, on land and sea, through their evil deeds. Others said: Rather, by land he meant the back of the earth, the cities and other things, and by sea he meant the well-known sea. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: Corruption has appeared on land and sea. He said: On land: the son of Adam who killed his brother, and at sea: the one who took every ship by force. Yaqub told me, he said: Abu Bishr said: meaning Ibn Ulayyah, he said: I heard Ibn Abi Nujayh say regarding His statement, Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned, he said: because of the killing of the son of Adam, and the one who used to seize every ship by force. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yazid ibn Harun told us, on the authority of Fadil ibn Marzuq, on the authority of Atiyyah, Corruption has appeared on land and sea. He said: I said: This is the land and sea, what corruption is there in it? He said: He said: When the rain decreases. He said: Diving. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told me, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Corruption has appeared on land, he said: The son of Adam killed his brother, and on the sea: he said: The king seized the ships by force. The most correct of the sayings is that God, the Most High, mentioned that corruption has appeared on land and sea among the Arabs in the barren lands. The sea is of two types: a salt sea and a freshwater sea. They consider them both to be seas. God, the Most High, did not specify that this appeared in one sea rather than another. So it depends on what the name sea refers to, whether it is freshwater or salty. If that is the case, then it includes the villages that are on rivers and seas. The interpretation of the statement then, since the matter was as you described: God’s sins appeared in every place, on land and sea, because of what the hands of people have earned: that is, because of the sins of people, and injustice spread in them. And His statement, That He may let them taste some of what they have done, means, the Most High, that He may afflict them with the punishment of some of the deeds they have done and the sins they have committed, that they may return, meaning that they may turn to the truth, return to repentance, and abandon the sins of God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Perhaps they will return. He said: They will repent. He said: Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, Perhaps they will return on the day of Badr, perhaps they will repent. He said: Abu Usama told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, Perhaps they will return. He said: To the truth. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, That He may let them taste some of what they have done, that perhaps they will return: Perhaps someone will return, perhaps someone who repents will repent, perhaps someone who seeks repentance will seek repentance. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Amir told us, he said: Qurra told us on the authority of Al-Hasan, Perhaps they will return. He said: He will return after them. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, li-yathiqhum. The majority of the reciters of the regions read it as li-yathiqhum with a ya, meaning: So that God may make them taste some of what they did. It was mentioned that Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Salami read it with a nun as a way of informing God about Himself with that.
30:42: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your al-Nas 114:Travel through the land and see the dwellings of those who disbelieved in God before you and denied His messengers. How was their final situation and the consequence of their denial of God’s messengers and their disbelief? Did We not destroy them with a punishment from Us and make them an example for those who came after them? Most of them were polytheists, meaning: We did that to them because most of them were polytheists like them.
30:43: God Almighty says: So turn your face, O Muhammad, toward the direction toward which your Lord has directed you, to the right religion, to obey your Lord, and the straight path in which there is no deviation from the truth, before there comes a Day from God of which there is no averting, God Almighty says: before the coming of a day from God of which there is no averting its coming, because God has decreed its coming, so it will inevitably come. On that Day they will be divided, meaning: on the day that comes, people will be divided, meaning: people will be divided into two groups, from their saying: the sheep divided into two groups: a group in Paradise, and a group in the Blaze. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, So direct your face toward the right religion means Islam, “before there comes from God a Day for which there is no repelling. On that Day they will be divided” A group in Paradise, and a group in the Blaze. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, On that Day they will be split apart, meaning: they will be scattered. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, They will be divided, he said: They will be divided into Paradise and Hell.
30:44: God Almighty says: Whoever disbelieves in God, then upon him is he, or his disbelief increases, and the sins of his ingratitude for the blessings of his Lord. And whoever does righteousness means: whoever obeys God, and does what He has commanded him to do in this world, and refrains from what He has forbidden him to do in it. Then for themselves they prepare means: for themselves they prepare, and they make their bed so that they may be safe from the punishment of their Lord, and escape His torment, as the poet said: Prepare yourself for illness and death, and do not waste a soul that has no successor. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that. Who said that? Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, For themselves they prepare he said: They make their beds. Ibn Al-Muthanna, Al-Hussein bin Yazid Al-Tahhan, Ibn Wakee’ and Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Ala’i told us: Yahya bin Salim told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: They prepare for themselves means in the grave. Ibrahim bin Saeed Al-Jawhari told us: Yahya bin Salim told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And for themselves they prepare He said: The grave. Nasr bin Ali told us, he said: Yahya bin Salim told us, he said: Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, he said: I heard Mujahid say: Regarding His statement, They prepare for themselves, it is said: in the grave.
30:45: God the Most High says: On that Day they will be separated… That He may reward those who believed in God and His Messenger and did righteous deeds meaning: and did what God commanded them out of His bounty which He promised to reward those who obeyed Him in this world on the Day of Resurrection Indeed, He does not like the disbelievers God the Most High says: He only singled out for His reward out of His bounty those who believed and did righteous deeds, not those who disbelieved in God. Indeed, He does not like the disbelievers in Him. He resumed the report by saying: Indeed, He does not like the disbelievers, and in it is the meaning that I described.
30:46: God Almighty says: And among His proofs of His Oneness and His arguments against you that He is the God of all things is that He sends the winds as good tidings of rain and mercy. And that He may let you taste of His mercy means: and that He may send down upon you of His mercy, which is the rain with which He revives the land, and that ships may sail in the seas by His command. And that you may seek of His bounty means: and that you may seek from His provisions and your livelihoods which He has apportioned among you. And that you may be grateful means: and that you may thank your Lord for that He sent these winds as good tidings. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, The winds are good tidings, he said: of rain. They said about His statement, And that He may let you taste of His mercy, the same as we said about it. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And that He may let you taste of His mercy, he said: rain. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And that He may let you taste of His mercy: rain.
30:47: God Almighty says, consoling His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the harm he suffered from his people, with what he suffered from His messengers before him from their people, and teaching him His way with them and their people, and that He will follow with him and his people His way with them and their nations: “And We sent, O Muhammad, messengers before you to their disbelieving people, just as We sent you to your people who worshipped idols instead of God. “And they came to them with clear proofs” meaning: with clear arguments proving their truthfulness and that they are messengers of God, just as you came to your people with clear proofs, but they denied them just as your people denied you, and they rejected what they brought them from God, just as they rejected what you brought them from your Lord. So We took retribution from those who committed crimes meaning: We took retribution from those who committed sins and acquired evil deeds from their people, and We will do the same to the criminals of your people. And it was incumbent upon Us to support the believers. He says, “And We saved those who believed in God and believed in His messengers, when Our punishment came to them. And thus We will deal with you and with those of your people who believed in you. And it was incumbent upon Us to support the believers” over the disbelievers. And We will support you and those who believed in Him against those who disbelieved in you, and We will make them victorious over you.
30:48: God the Most High says: God sends the winds, and they stir up clouds. He says: So the winds create clouds, which is the plural of cloud, and He spreads them out in the sky as He wills. He says: So God spreads them out and gathers them in the sky as He wills. He said: He spreads them out, so He made the ha’ singular and used it as a metaphor for the masculine, and clouds are plural as I described in response to the word clouds, not to its meaning, as one says: These are good dates. And in a similar manner to what we said in the interpretation of His statement, He extends it, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: He spreads it out in the sky as He wills and gathers it. And His saying, And He makes it into fragments, means: And He makes the clouds into scattered pieces. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And He makes it an eclipse: meaning, a cut-off. His saying, Then you will see the drizzle, meaning the rain, coming out of it, meaning from between the clouds. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then you will see the rain emerging from within it. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Qatan, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Ubaid ibn Umair, He sends the winds and they stir up the clouds. He said: The winds are four: God sends a wind that makes the earth swell, then God sends a second wind that stirs up clouds and makes them scattered in the sky, then God sends a third wind that brings them together and makes them heaps, then He sends a fourth wind that causes rain. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Then you will see the rain, he said: the rain. And His statement, Then when He sends it down upon whomever He wills of His servants, at once they rejoice, means: So when He directs that rain to the land of whomever He wills to direct it from among His creation, you will see them rejoicing that He directed that to them and they will be happy.
30:49: God Almighty says: And these servants whom God afflicted with this rain before He sent down this rain upon them were in despair, meaning: they were depressed and sad because of its withholding from them. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And they were, before it was sent down to them, in despair. That is, they were hopeless. The Arab scholars differed on the reason for repeating min qabdhu before it was sent down upon them (ar-Rum 30:49). Some of the Basran grammarians said: Min qabdhu was repeated for emphasis, like his saying: So the angels prostrated themselves, all of them together (ar-Hijr 15:30 - 73). Another said: That is not the case, because with “min qabdhu an nasalu there is a letter that is not with the second one. He said: “So it is as if he said: before the sending down, before the rain,” so they differed. As for all of them together, it was emphasized with all of them together because each can be a noun and it can be an emphasis, which is his saying all of them. And the opinion, in my opinion, is regarding his saying min qabdhu for emphasis.
30:50: The reciters differed regarding his statement, So look at the traces of God’s mercy. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufians, recited it as to the traces of God’s mercy in the singular, meaning: So look, O Muhammad, at the traces of the rain that God has bestowed upon whomever He has afflicted among His servants, how that rain revives the earth after its death. The majority of the Kufian reciters recited it as So look at the traces of God’s mercy in the plural, meaning: So look at the traces of the rain that God has bestowed upon whomever He has afflicted, how He revives the earth after its death. The correct statement in this regard is that they are two well-known readings in the readings of the regions, and they are close in meaning. This is because when God revives the earth with rain that He sends down upon it, then the rain revives it by God reviving it with it. And when the rain revives it, then God is the One who revives with it. So whichever of the two readings the reader recites, he is correct. The interpretation of the statement then is: Look, O Muhammad, at the traces of the rain that God sends down from the clouds, how He revives the dead earth with it, causing it to sprout and become green after its death and destruction. Indeed, that is the One who revives the dead. God, the Most High, says: Indeed, He who revives this earth after its death with this rain will revive the dead after their death. And He is over all things competent, along with His ability to revive the dead. Nothing He wills is too difficult for Him, and nothing He wills is impossible for Him to do, glory be to Him.
30:51: God Almighty says: And if We sent a corrupting wind, what the rain which We sent down from the sky would not have grown, and those whom God afflicted with that rain by which their land was revived, and by which their crops grew, saw what their land had grown by that rain, yellowed, spoiled by that wind which We sent, and it had turned yellow after it had been green, they would have remained, after their rejoicing and happiness at it, disbelieving in their Lord.
30:52: God Almighty says, For you, O Muhammad, do not make the dead hear. He says: Do not give them ears by which they can understand what you say to them. This is an example of its meaning: For you are not able to make these polytheists understand, whose hearing God has sealed, and thus deprived them of understanding the admonitions of His revelation that are recited to them, just as you are not able to make the dead understand, whose hearing God has deprived, by giving them ears. And His statement, And the deaf cannot hear the call, means: Just as you cannot make the deaf who have been deprived of hearing hear the call, if they turn away from you and depart, likewise you cannot help those whom God has deprived of understanding the verses of His Book, to hear and understand that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, For indeed you cannot make the dead hear: this is a parable that God gave for the disbeliever. Just as the dead cannot hear the call, so too the disbeliever cannot hear. And the deaf cannot hear the call when they turn their backs and depart means: If a deaf person turned their backs and you called him, he would not hear. Likewise the disbeliever does not hear nor benefit from what he hears.
30:53: And His statement, And you cannot guide the blind from their misguidance, the Most High says: And you, O Muhammad, cannot guide one whom God has blinded from the straight path and the path of truth, and has not granted him success in finding the right path, and has not diverted him from his misguidance which he is upon, and his unjust riding of the paths, to the path of right guidance. He says: That is not in your hand nor is it up to you, and no one has the power to do that except Me, because I am the One who has power over all things. And it was said: He can guide the blind from their misguidance, and He did not say: From their misguidance. Because the meaning of the statement is what I described, that it is: And you cannot divert them from it, so it was carried on the meaning. If it had been said: From their misguidance, it would have been correct. And its meaning would have been: You cannot prevent them from their misguidance. And His statement, None hears except he who believes in Our verses, the Most High says to His Prophet: You do not hear the hearing from which its listener benefits and understands it, except he who believes in Our verses, because the one who believes in Our verses, if he hears the Book of God, ponders it, understands it, and understands it, and acts according to what is in it, and adheres to the limits of God, which He has set in it, then he is the one who hears the beneficial hearing. His saying, They are Muslims, means that they are submissive to God in their obedience to Him, and humbled by the admonitions of His Book.
30:54: God Almighty says to these polytheists of Quraysh who denied the resurrection, arguing with them that He is able to do that and do whatever He wills. God is He who created you O people from weakness meaning: from clean, despised water, then produced you as well-proportioned human beings. Then, after weakness, He made strength meaning: Then He gave you the strength to act, after He created you from weakness, and after your weakness in youth and childhood. Then, after strength, He made weakness and gray hair meaning: Then He created for you weakness through old age and decrepitude, compared to when you were strong in your youth and gray hair. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Who created you from weakness means from a sperm-drop, Then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness old age and gray hair is the hairy hair. And His statement, He creates what He wills, means that the Most High says: He creates what He wills of weakness and strength, youth and old age. And He is the All-Knowing of the management of His creation. The All-Powerful over what He wills. Nothing He wills is impossible for Him. Just as He did these things, so too He causes His creation to die and brings them to life whenever He wills. He says: Know that the One who performed these actions with His power will bring the dead to life whenever He wills.
30:55: God the Most High says: And on the Day the Hour of Resurrection comes, and creation is resurrected from their graves, the criminals will swear - they are those who disbelieved in God in this world and committed sins therein - and their oath is their oath by God, They did not remain but an hour: meaning, they will swear that they did not remain in their graves more than one hour. God the Most High says: Thus in this world they were lying: meaning, they lied in their saying and their oath, We did not remain but an hour, just as they used to lie and swear lies in this world while they knew. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: “And on the Day the Hour will come, the criminals will swear that they had not remained [in the world] except for an hour. Thus they were deluded.” That is, they lied in this world. What he means by his saying deluded is about truthfulness and turning away from it to falsehood.
30:56: Qatada used to say: This is from the word al-muqaddam which means al-tadda’. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And those who were given knowledge and faith said, ‘You have indeed remained in the Book of God until the Day of Resurrection.’ He said: This is one of the basic principles of speech. Its interpretation is: And those who were given faith and knowledge said, ‘You have indeed remained in the Book of God until the Day of Resurrection.’” It was reported on the authority of Ibn Jurayj that he used to say: The meaning of this is: And those who were given knowledge of the Book of God and faith in God and His Book said. And his saying, In the Book of God, he says: In what God wrote, what He previously knew that you would remain there. This is the Day of Resurrection, he says: This is the day when people will be resurrected from their graves. But you did not know, he says: But you did not know in this world that it would happen, and that you would be resurrected after death, and that is why you were lying.
30:57: God Almighty says: On the Day they are resurrected from their graves, Their excuse will not benefit those who did wrong. That is, those who denied the resurrection in this world, their excuses, which is their saying: We did not know that it would happen, nor that we would be resurrected. “Nor will they be asked to repent.” That is, these wrongdoers will not be asked to turn back on that day for what they denied in this world.
30:58: God Almighty says: And We have certainly given the people in this Qur'an every kind of example as an argument against them and a warning to them about the Oneness of God. And His statement, And if you bring them a sign, means: And if you, O Muhammad, bring these people a sign, meaning: as evidence of the truth of what you say, those who disbelieve will surely say, ‘You are not but falsifiers,’ meaning those who denied your message and rejected your prophethood will surely say: You, O believers in what Muhammad has brought you, are not but falsifiers in what you bring us of these matters.
30:59: God Almighty says: Thus does God seal the hearts of those who do not know the truth of what you bring them, O Muhammad, from God of these lessons, sermons, and clear signs. So they do not understand God’s argument, nor do they comprehend what He recites to them from the verses of His Book. Therefore, they hesitate in their transgression.
30:60: God the Almighty says: So be patient, O Muhammad, when they harm you, and convey to them the message of your Lord, for the promise of God which He promised you of victory over them, and triumph over them, and the empowerment of you and your companions and followers in the land is true. And do not let those who have no certainty discourage you meaning: And do not let these polytheists who do not believe in the afterlife and do not believe in the resurrection after death discourage you from the command of God and the fulfillment of what He has charged you with, which is conveying His message to them. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ali bin Rabi’ah, that a man from the Khawarij recited after Ali, may God be pleased with him: If you should associate others with God, your work will surely become worthless, and you will surely be among the losers (al-Zumar 39:65). Ali said: “So be patient. Indeed, the promise of God is truth. And do not let those who have no certainty make you impatient.” He said: Yahya bin Adam narrated to us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Uthman bin Abi Zar’ah, on the authority of Ali bin Rabi’ah, who said: A man from the Khawarij called out to Ali, may God be pleased with him, while he was praying Fajr, and said: And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you that if you should associate others with God, your work would surely become worthless, and you would surely be among the losers. (al-Zumar 39:65) So Ali, may God be pleased with him, answered him while he was praying: “So be patient. Indeed, the promise of God is truth. And do not let those who have no certainty make you impatient.” Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, “So be patient. Indeed, the promise of God is truth. And do not let those who have no certainty make you impatient.” He said: A man from the Khawarij said to Ali during the morning prayer, And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you that if you should associate others with God, your work would surely become worthless, and you would surely be among the losers. (al-Zumar 39:65). Ali, may God be pleased with him, listened to him until he understood what he said, then he answered him while he was praying, “So be patient. Indeed, the promise of God is truth. And do not let those who have no certainty make you impatient.”
